questions.question: A computer that processes discrete signals is called ____.
questions.explanation: A digital computer works with discrete (separate, countable) values, usually 0s and 1s. Option E, an analog computer, works with continuous signals such as voltage or temperature, and option A, a hybrid computer, combines both types.

questions.question: The computer can perform the following operations except
questions.explanation: A flowchart is a diagram people draw to plan the steps of a solution, not an operation the computer carries out. Jump, shift, computing and comparing (options A, C, D and E) are all basic operations a computer's processor can perform.

questions.question: The basic operations performed by a computer are
questions.explanation: A computer performs arithmetic operations, logical operations, and the storage and retrieval of data. Since options A, B and C are each basic operations, option D, all of them, is correct.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a mainframe and a super computer?

options.a: Super computer is much larger than mainframe computers
options.b: Super computers are much smaller than mainframe computers
options.c: Supercomputers are focused to execute few programs as fast as possible while mainframe uses its power to execute as many programs concurrently
options.d: Supercomputers are focused to execute as many programs as possible while mainframe uses its power to execute few programs as fast as possible.

questions.explanation: A supercomputer focuses its power on running a few programs as fast as possible, often for heavy scientific calculations. A mainframe instead serves very many users and programs at the same time. Option D swaps these roles, and options A and B are about size, which is not the main difference.

questions.question: Computer is free from tiredness and boredom. We call it
questions.explanation: Diligence means a computer can work for long periods without tiredness or boredom, keeping the same speed and accuracy. Option A, accuracy, is about producing correct results. Option D, versatility, is about doing many different kinds of tasks.

questions.question: A hybrid computer

options.c: Resembles both a digital and analogue computer

questions.explanation: A hybrid computer combines features of both digital and analog computers, so it can handle continuous and discrete data together. Options A and B each describe only one side of it.

questions.question: One millisecond is
questions.explanation: Milli means one thousandth, so 1 millisecond = 1/1000 second = 0.001 s. Option B, one tenth of a second, would be a decisecond. Option D, one ten-thousandth, is ten times smaller than a millisecond.

questions.question: A modern electronic computer is a machine that is meant for

options.b: Input, storage, manipulation and outputting of data

questions.explanation: A modern computer is designed to accept input, store it, manipulate (process) it and produce output. Options A, C and D each describe only part of what a computer does, while option B covers the whole input-process-output-storage cycle.

questions.question: Properly arranged data is called
questions.explanation: Data that has been processed and arranged in a meaningful way is called information. Options A and D, field and file, are units for storing data. Option B, words, are groups of bits or characters.

questions.question: Once you load the suitable program and provide required data, computer does not need human intervention. This feature is known as
questions.explanation: Automation means that once the program and data are loaded, the computer carries out the task by itself without human help. Option B, reliability, is about producing consistent results. Option C, versatility, is about doing many different jobs.

questions.question: What is a brand?

options.a: The name of companies that made computers
options.b: The name of product a company gives to identify its product in market
options.c: A name of class to indicate all similar products from different companies

questions.explanation: A brand is the name a company gives its product so buyers can recognise it in the market. Option A, the company's name, is not always the brand. Option C describes a product category, not a brand.

questions.question: Modern Computers are very reliable but they are not
questions.explanation: Computers are very reliable but not infallible: they can still give wrong results if they receive wrong data or faulty programs ('garbage in, garbage out'). Options A and B are wrong because computers are fast and powerful. Option D is not the point of the statement.

questions.question: Computer operators

options.a: writes computer programs for specific problems
options.b: operate the device which input and output data from the computer
options.c: normally require a college degree in computer science

questions.explanation: Computer operators run the computer and its input and output devices. Option A, writing programs, is the job of programmers, and option C is wrong because operators do not normally need a computer science degree.

questions.question: ____ computers are also called personal computers
questions.explanation: Microcomputers, built around a microprocessor, are also called personal computers because they are designed for one user at a time. Options A, B and D, mainframes, minicomputers and supercomputers, are larger systems that serve many users or special tasks.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is false?

options.a: Mechanical analog computers have existed for thousands of years
options.b: There are mechanical analog computers and electronic analog computers.
options.c: All electronic computers are digital computers

questions.explanation: The false statement is that all electronic computers are digital: electronic analog computers also exist, as option B says. Option A is true because mechanical analog devices are very old, so option D is wrong.

questions.question: Analog computer works on the supply of
questions.explanation: An analog computer works with continuous signals, such as smoothly varying voltages, rather than separate on/off pulses. Option B, non-continuous pulses, describes how a digital computer works. Option C, magnetic strength, is not its basis.

questions.question: One computer that is not considered a portable is
questions.explanation: A minicomputer is a mid-sized machine meant to sit in an office or computer room serving many users, so it is not portable. Laptop and notebook computers (options B and C) are designed to be carried around, which rules out option D as well.

questions.question: Which is the largest computer?
questions.explanation: Supercomputers are the largest and most powerful class of computers, often filling whole rooms with thousands of processors. Option A, the mainframe, is large too, but it comes below the supercomputer in size and power; minis and micros (B and C) are smaller still.

questions.question: What is meant by a dedicated computer?

options.a: Which is used by one person only
options.b: Which is assigned one and only one task
options.c: Which uses one kind of software
options.d: Which is meant for application software

questions.explanation: A dedicated computer is set aside to perform one specific job only, such as controlling a machine or running a single system. Option A confuses dedicated with single-user, and options C and D describe software choices rather than a dedicated purpose.

questions.question: Which is the highest form?
questions.explanation: Data are raw facts, information is processed data, and knowledge is information that has been understood and applied, so knowledge is the highest form. Options A and B are lower levels in this hierarchy, so option D cannot be right.

questions.question: What produces useful information out of data?
questions.explanation: Processing is the act of working on raw data, by sorting, calculating or summarising it, to turn it into useful information. Option A, the computer, is the tool that does the processing, and option C, programming, is writing the instructions, not producing the information itself.

questions.question: A digital computer did not score over an analog computer in terms of
questions.explanation: Analog computers work on continuous signals and give results almost instantly, so they are generally faster than digital computers. Digital computers score over analog ones in accuracy and reliability, which is why options B and C are wrong.

questions.question: A computer has very low failure rate because it uses electronic components. It produces very consistent results. This is highlighted by which of the feature of computer?
questions.explanation: Reliability means a computer rarely fails and keeps producing consistent results, thanks to its long-lasting electronic components. Option A, accuracy, is about results being correct, and option C, versatility, is about doing many different kinds of work.

questions.question: The act of retrieving existing data from memory is called
questions.explanation: Getting existing data out of memory can be called a read, a read-out or reading from memory; all three terms describe the same action. Because each of options A, B and C is an accepted term, option D is the best answer.

questions.question: Which of the following is valid statement?

options.a: Data in itself is useless unless it is processed
options.b: The data that is processed is called a program
options.c: The data which is not yet processed is information
options.d: Information is processed by computer to generate data.

questions.explanation: Raw data has little value until it is processed into meaningful information. Option B is wrong because processed data is information, not a program, and options C and D reverse the relationship between data and information.

questions.question: Personnel who design, program, operates and maintains computer equipment refers to
questions.explanation: Peopleware (also called humanware or liveware) refers to all the people who design, program, operate and maintain computer systems. Options A, B and D each name only one type of computer worker, not the whole group.

questions.question: Regarding data, computers are very good at
questions.explanation: Computers are very good at storing huge amounts of data, processing it quickly and retrieving it when needed. Since each of options A, B and C is a real strength, option D is correct.

questions.question: The term GIGO is related to
questions.explanation: GIGO means Garbage In, Garbage Out: a computer's results are only as accurate as the data and instructions it is given, so it relates to accuracy. Options B and C, reliability and versatility, are about failure rates and doing many tasks, not correctness of output.

questions.question: Digital devices are

options.c: Clock with a dial and two hands

questions.explanation: A digital clock shows time as separate numbers that jump from one value to the next, which makes it a digital device. A speedometer with a needle and a clock with hands (B and C) show continuously changing values, so they are analog devices.

questions.question: After copying the content how many times can you paste?
questions.explanation: Copied content stays on the clipboard until something else is copied, so you can paste it as many times as you like. Options A, B and C wrongly suggest a fixed limit.

questions.question: The term 'computer' is derived from
questions.explanation: The word computer comes from the Latin word computare, meaning to calculate or reckon. Greek, Sanskrit and German (A, B and D) are not its origin.

questions.question: Which of the following term means to reckon?
questions.explanation: The Latin verb putare means to reckon or think, and joined with com (together) it forms computare, the root of the word computer. Option B, com, only means together, and options C and D are pieces or altered forms of computare rather than the word that means to reckon.

questions.question: Computer professionals working in a computer centre are
questions.explanation: Humanware (also called liveware or peopleware) refers to the people who work with computers, such as operators, programmers and analysts. Software, firmware and hardware (A, B and C) are programs and physical equipment, not people.

questions.question: The qualitative or quantitative attribute of a variable or set of variables is termed as
questions.explanation: Data are the raw qualitative or quantitative values of a variable, such as names, numbers or measurements. Information (option B) is what you get after processing that data, so option C is not correct.

questions.question: By programmable machine we mean

options.d: anything that can be set to perform different tasks with suitable programs

questions.explanation: A programmable machine is anything that can be set to do different jobs by giving it different programs. Option A names computers, which are only one example, so option D is the full meaning; options B and C are just other examples.

questions.question: Identify the true statement

options.a: Computers process data accurately, but wrong input still gives wrong output (GIGO)
options.b: Computers are reliable because they use electronic component which have very low failure rate
options.c: Computer is never tired and does not suffer from boredom

questions.explanation: All three statements are true. Computers process data accurately, but if the input is wrong the output will also be wrong (garbage in, garbage out); they are reliable because electronic parts rarely fail; and they never get tired or bored. Since A, B and C are all true, D is the answer.

questions.question: The proper definition of a modern digital computer is

options.a: An electronic automated machine that can solve problems involving words and numbers
options.b: A more sophisticated and modified electronic pocket calculator
options.c: Any machine that can perform mathematical operations
options.d: A machine that works on binary code

questions.explanation: A modern digital computer is an electronic, automatic, programmable machine that can solve problems involving both words and numbers. Option B makes it just a pocket calculator, option C would include simple adding machines, and option D is too narrow a description.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most powerful computers?
questions.explanation: Supercomputers are the most powerful computers, able to carry out enormous numbers of calculations per second for tasks such as weather forecasting. Mainframes, minis and micros (A, B and C) are progressively less powerful.

questions.question: Raw facts and figures about any particular topic are
questions.explanation: Data are raw, unprocessed facts and figures about a topic. Information (option A) is what you get after the data has been processed and given meaning.

questions.question: A computer can solve more than one kind of problem. This is related to which of the following characteristics?
questions.explanation: Versatility means a computer can be used for many different kinds of tasks, from calculations to games to word processing. Options A and B, accuracy and reliability, are about correct results and low failure rates, not variety.

questions.question: In analog computer

options.a: Input is first converted to digital form
options.b: Input is never converted to digital form
options.c: Output is displayed in digital form

questions.explanation: An analog computer works directly with continuously varying quantities such as voltage or pressure, so its input is never converted to digital form. Options A and C describe digital computers.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a form of data?
questions.explanation: Numbers, characters, images and sound can all be stored and processed as data by a computer. Since options A, B and C are all forms of data, option D, none of the above, is correct.

questions.question: Which is not a computer classification?
questions.explanation: Maxframe is not a real computer category. Mainframe, minicomputer and notebook (options A, C and D) are all recognised classes of computer.

questions.question: Which operation is not performed by computer
questions.explanation: Computers can take input, process data and control devices, but they do not truly understand what they are doing; they simply follow instructions. Options A, B and C are all operations a computer performs.

questions.question: On which aspect the analog computers are better than digital?
questions.explanation: Analog computers work on continuous signals and give results almost instantly, so their main advantage over digital computers is speed. Digital computers are the more accurate and reliable ones, which rules out options B and C.

questions.question: The subject of cybernetics deals with the science of
questions.explanation: Cybernetics is the science of control and communication in machines and living things, studying how systems use feedback to regulate themselves. Genetics, molecular biology and biochemistry (A, C, D) are branches of biology, not the study of control systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a micro computer?
questions.explanation: Laptops, tablets and desktop PCs are all microcomputers, because each is built around a single microprocessor and meant for one user. Since A, B and C all are microcomputers, the correct choice is D, none of the above.

questions.question: Signals can be analog or digital and a computer that processes the both type of signals is known as
questions.explanation: A hybrid computer combines analog and digital features, so it can handle both continuous (analog) and discrete (digital) signals. Analog and digital computers (A, B) each handle only one type, and mainframe (D) describes size, not signal type.

questions.question: Human beings are referred to as Homo sapiens, which device is called Silico sapiens?
questions.explanation: Silico sapiens is a playful name for the computer, a 'wise' machine built from silicon chips, just as Homo sapiens names the wise human. A monitor (A) and hardware (B) are only parts of a computer, and a robot (C) is just one application of one.

questions.question: Number cruncher is the informal name for
questions.explanation: A supercomputer is nicknamed a number cruncher because it performs huge amounts of numerical calculation very fast, for jobs like weather forecasting. Mini, micro and mainframe computers (A, C, D) are not described by that informal name.

questions.question: Which of the following is a class of computers based on model?
questions.explanation: Classifying by model groups PCs into types such as XT, AT and PS/2, so AT computers belong to a model-based class. Digital, hybrid and analog computers (A, B, C) are classified by how they work, not by model.

questions.question: What are the computers called that performs calculations and comparisons usually in the binary numbering system?
questions.explanation: Digital computers work with discrete values, usually in binary (0s and 1s), to perform calculations and comparisons. Analog computers (A) work with continuous quantities, and hybrid computers (C) mix both approaches.

questions.question: An example of a digital device can be

options.c: Clock with a dial and two hands

questions.explanation: A digital clock shows time as discrete numbers, which makes it a digital device. A car speedometer and a clock with hands (B, C) show continuously moving values, which makes them analog devices.

questions.question: Which of the following have low failure rate?
questions.explanation: Electronic devices have no moving parts to wear out, so they fail much less often. Mechanical and electro-mechanical devices (A, C) depend on moving parts that wear and break.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a class based on size?
questions.explanation: Digital is a class based on how a computer works (with discrete values), not on its size. Mainframe, micro and mini computers (A, B, C) are all size-based classes.

questions.question: Which of the following professions has not been affected by personal computers?
questions.explanation: Personal computers have affected nearly every profession, including medicine, clerical and legal work, and accounting. Since A, B and C have all been affected, the answer is D.

questions.question: Which computers are used as servers for any medium sized organizations?
questions.explanation: Minicomputers are mid-sized multi-user machines that are well suited to serving a medium-sized organization. Mainframes and supercomputers (A, D) are aimed at very large organizations or heavy computing, while microcomputers (C) are mainly single-user machines.

questions.question: All modern computer operate on
questions.explanation: Computers operate on data: they accept raw facts, process them and produce information. Information (A) is the result of processing, not what the computer takes in, and floppies and words (B, D) are a medium and a unit.

questions.question: When we look at the cost, which of the following computer is most expensive?
questions.explanation: Supercomputers are the most expensive class of computers because they are built for extreme speed with thousands of processors. Mainframes (A) are costly but cheaper than supercomputers, and mini and micro computers (B, C) cost far less.

questions.question: The computer that process both analog and digital is called
questions.explanation: A hybrid computer processes both analog and digital data by combining features of both types. Analog and digital computers (A, B) handle only one type, and mainframe (D) describes size.

questions.question: Which of the following class of computers can process physical quantities such as speed?
questions.explanation: Analog computers work with continuously changing physical quantities like speed, temperature and pressure. Digital computers (B) work with discrete numbers, and hybrid computers (C) combine both, so A is the class built for this.

questions.question: One computer that is not considered a portable computer is
questions.explanation: A minicomputer is a mid-sized multi-user machine that sits in one place, so it is not portable. Laptops and tablet PCs (B, C) are portable computers, so D is wrong.

questions.question: In what respect human beings are superior to computers?
questions.explanation: Humans are superior to computers in intelligence: we can think, reason and use judgment, while computers only follow instructions. Diligence and reliability (A, D) are areas where computers are stronger, and 'slavery' (C) is not a real advantage.

questions.question: CAD stands for
questions.explanation: CAD stands for Computer Aided Design, the use of computers to create and change designs and technical drawings. 'Algorithm for design' and 'application in design' (B, C) are not the correct expansion.

questions.question: A computer that has no disk or diskette drive of its own, and loads its programs and data from a server over a network, is called a
questions.explanation: A diskless computer has no disk drive of its own, so it starts up and gets its programs and data from a server over a network. Home computers (A), dedicated computers (C) and general purpose computers (D) describe what a computer is used for, not whether it has a disk drive.

questions.question: Which of the following class of computers can not support multiple users simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Microcomputers, such as personal computers, are designed to be used by one person at a time. Mainframes (A) and minicomputers (B) are built to serve many users at once through connected terminals, so D is wrong as well.

questions.question: A factor which would strongly influence a business person to adopt a computer is its
questions.explanation: Businesses adopt computers because they work fast, give accurate results and perform reliably over and over. Accuracy (A), reliability (B) and speed (C) are each important benefits, so all of them together is the best answer.

questions.question: In what respect computers are superior to human beings?
questions.explanation: Diligence means a computer can work for long hours without getting tired, bored or losing concentration, which makes it better than humans at repetitive work. Computers do not have intelligence (B) of their own; they only follow instructions, so C is wrong too.

questions.question: Com in Latin is

options.c: a term that means to reckon

questions.explanation: The word computer comes from the Latin computare, made of com- (a prefix meaning together, often used to intensify) and putare (to reckon or think). So com is a prefix, not a suffix (B), and the part that means to reckon is putare, not com (C).

questions.question: Which of the following is not a classification of computers based on the type of data they handle?
questions.explanation: By the type of data they handle, computers are classed as analog (continuous quantities), digital (discrete values) and hybrid (both). Electronic is not one of these classes, because analog, digital and hybrid computers can all be electronic, so A is the answer.

questions.question: Which basic operation below can a computer perform?
questions.explanation: A computer can calculate, compare or test values, shift data and jump to other instructions, because these are all basic operations built into its processor. Since B, C, D and E are each correct, All of the above is the best answer.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a computer?

options.a: To retain data indefinitely in storage
options.b: To transform data into usable information
options.c: To generate hard copies of documents

questions.explanation: A computer's main job is to accept data and process it into useful information. Storing data (A), printing documents (C) and connecting to networks (D) are things computers can do, but they support that main purpose rather than being it.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a computer?
questions.explanation: Computers only follow the instructions they are given, so they cannot think creatively or come up with original solutions. Speed (A), accuracy (B) and storage (D) are all real characteristics of computers.

questions.question: The term "computer" originally referred to:
questions.explanation: Before electronic machines existed, a computer was a person whose job was to do calculations by hand. The meaning later shifted to the electronic devices (A) that took over that work.

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of using computers?
questions.explanation: Computers automate repetitive operations, saving time and reducing human effort. Options A, B and D describe drawbacks, not benefits, because computers reduce manual work, increase efficiency and store large amounts of data.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of computer based on size?
questions.explanation: Computers are grouped by size into supercomputers, mainframes, minicomputers and microcomputers, and a mainframe is a large computer for big processing jobs. Operating systems (B), application suites (C) and coding languages (D) are kinds of software, not sizes of computers.

questions.question:
A computer system can be described as
i an electronic device
ii a device that cannot be programmed
iii a mechanical device
iv a device for carrying data
v a device for storing and processing data
vi a device that works based on some given logic
questions.explanation: A computer is an electronic device (i) that stores and processes data (v) by following given logic, that is, the instructions in a program (vi). Statement ii is false because computers are programmable, iii is wrong because modern computers are electronic rather than mechanical, and iv is wrong because simply carrying data is not what defines a computer. Option D is tempting, but it includes the false statement ii.

questions.question: Example of analog device is
questions.explanation: An analog device measures quantities that change continuously, such as speed, and a traditional speedometer shows this with a needle moving smoothly over a dial. Laptops, smartphones and hard disks (options A, B and C) store and process data as discrete binary digits, so they are digital devices.

questions.question: Arrange the computers according to their processing power

options.c: They all have same processing power

questions.explanation: Supercomputers are the most powerful, followed by mainframes, then minicomputers, and microcomputers (personal computers) are the least powerful. Options A and B put these categories in the wrong order, and C is false because the categories differ greatly in processing power.

questions.question: Digital computers ______ things
questions.explanation: Digital computers work with discrete digits, so they count, while analogue computers measure continuously changing quantities such as temperature or speed. That makes "measure" (A) the job of analogue computers, not digital ones.

questions.question: Computers may be classified by size. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: By size, computers are grouped as micro (including notebooks and laptops), mini, mainframe and super computers. Notebook, mini and mainframe all describe sizes, so C is correct. A, B and D are wrong because they mix in "digital" or "analogue", which describe how a computer works, not its size.

questions.question: Computer system is different from a calculator because the computer contains
questions.explanation: What sets a computer apart from a calculator is that it runs stored software under the direction of a control unit, so it can carry out a long sequence of instructions automatically. Calculators also have input and output parts (A) and a processor with a display (C), so those are not the difference.

questions.question: In terms of data representation, computer can be classified into the following

options.b: Analog, special purpose and general purpose

questions.explanation: By the way they represent data, computers are grouped as analog (continuous quantities), digital (discrete digits) and hybrid (a mix of both). Terms like special-purpose, general-purpose and programmable in options A, B, C and E describe what a computer is used for, not how it represents data.

questions.question: Why are mainframe computers housed in special facilities? Because
questions.explanation: Mainframes generate a lot of heat and are sensitive to dust and humidity, so they are kept in special rooms with controlled temperature and air. Their cost (B) does not by itself require a special facility, and they do not have any 'special power' (A).

questions.question: Analog computers ______ things
questions.explanation: Analog computers measure continuously changing quantities such as temperature, pressure or speed. Counting (B) is what digital computers do with discrete digits.

questions.question: Most general purpose computers can perform almost any task why?
questions.explanation: A general-purpose computer can do almost any task because it is programmable: give it a different program and it does a different job. Being fast or powerful (A, C) helps, but without programmability a machine is limited to a fixed task.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a digital computer

options.b: Input, memory, processor and stored program only
options.c: Input, memory, processor and output only
options.d: Input, memory, processor, stored program, output

questions.explanation: A digital computer is fully described by input, memory, a processor, a stored program and output, all working together. The other options each leave something out, such as output or the stored program, which is what makes a modern computer work.

questions.question: A hybrid computer consists of
questions.explanation: A hybrid computer combines the features of analog and digital computers: it measures continuous quantities like an analog machine and processes them with digital accuracy. Options A, B, C and E pair up computer sizes, which has nothing to do with being hybrid.

questions.question: Which of the following is true

options.a: Computers can solve all business problems.
options.d: Output from computer is always accurate

questions.explanation: Many modern computer systems use artificial intelligence, which is why C is the best choice here. The others are false: computers cannot solve every business problem (A), they have no natural intelligence (B), and their output is only as accurate as the input and program allow (D), as the phrase 'garbage in, garbage out' reminds us.

questions.question: Computer virus is a

options.c: Disease that enters into the computer through the air
options.d: Virus transmitted from people working with computer

questions.explanation: A computer virus is a harmful program that copies itself and spreads to other files and computers, often damaging data. It is not a living germ (A), and it does not pass between people and machines like a disease (C, D).

questions.question: Analog computers are widely used for
questions.explanation: Analog computers work with continuous quantities, which makes them well suited to simulation, for example modelling how a system such as an aircraft or a chemical process behaves. Database reports, regression and factor analysis (A, D, E) are digital, data-processing tasks.

questions.question: The digital computer has an edge over the analog in the following area:
questions.explanation: Digital computers work with exact digits, so they give precise, accurate results, while analog computers depend on physical measurements that are only approximate. Analog machines can actually be very fast at their particular tasks, so speed (A) is not the main advantage.

questions.question: The motorcar speedometer is a miniature
questions.explanation: A speedometer gives a continuous reading of speed through a needle that moves smoothly, which is exactly how an analog computer works: it measures. A digital device (B) would count and show discrete numbers.

questions.question: Most accounting software packages will run on
questions.explanation: Accounting packages work with exact figures, so they run on digital computers, which are the PCs and servers businesses use. Analog and hybrid computers (A, C) are built for measuring continuous quantities, not for business record keeping.

questions.question: What makes the computer different from other data processing machines?
questions.explanation: The stored program concept, keeping both the program instructions and the data in memory, lets a computer carry out a whole series of steps automatically. Other machines may have displays, storage or punch cards (B, D, E) but cannot follow a stored set of instructions by themselves.

questions.question: The period of ____ generation was from 1952-1964.
questions.explanation: The years 1952-1964 fall in the transistor era, which is the second generation of computers, coming after the vacuum-tube machines of the late 1940s and 1950s. Option B, the first generation, is the vacuum-tube era that this period follows, and option C, the third generation, is the integrated-circuit era that begins around the mid-1960s.

questions.question: The memory of the second generation of computers was built using ____.
questions.explanation: Second generation computers mostly used magnetic core memory, made of tiny magnetised rings, as their main memory. Option E, transistors, is the tempting choice, but transistors replaced vacuum tubes in the processing circuits, not in the memory. Option A, vacuum tubes, belongs to the first generation and option C, integrated circuits, to the third.

questions.question: The first true adding machine was invented in what year?
questions.explanation: Blaise Pascal built his adding machine, the Pascaline, in 1642, and it is regarded as the first true mechanical adding machine. Options A, B and E are close dates meant to confuse you, and option C, 1462, is far too early.

questions.question: In this generation, time-sharing, real-time, networks, and distributed operating systems were used.
questions.explanation: Time-sharing, real-time networks and distributed operating systems are listed as features of fourth generation computers, the microprocessor era that also brought network facilities and microcomputers. Option C, fifth generation, is tempting but is mainly linked to artificial intelligence and parallel processing. Option E, third generation, is when operating systems and multiprogramming were first introduced.

questions.question: The first electronic digital computers were developed in the
questions.explanation: The first electronic digital computers, such as the ABC and ENIAC (1946), were built in the 1940s using vacuum tubes. Option C, the 1960s, is the era of integrated circuits, well after the first electronic machines. Option A, the 1900s, is before any electronic computer existed.

questions.question: UNIVAC is
questions.explanation: UNIVAC stands for Universal Automatic Computer, the first commercial computer delivered to the U.S. Census Bureau in 1951. Options B, C and D change one word and are not real expansions.

questions.question: Microprocessors as switching devices are for which generation computers
questions.explanation: Fourth generation computers are based on the microprocessor, a whole CPU built on a single VLSI chip. Option A, the first generation, used vacuum tubes, option B, the second, used transistors, and option C, the third, used integrated circuits.

questions.question: Integrated Circuits (ICs) are related to which generation of computers?
questions.explanation: Integrated circuits (ICs) replaced transistors in the third generation of computers. Option A, the first generation, used vacuum tubes, and option B, the second, used transistors. Option D, the fourth generation, used VLSI chips and microprocessors.

questions.question: Which of the following IC was used in third generation of computers?
questions.explanation: Third generation computers used small-scale integration (SSI) and medium-scale integration (MSI) chips, so option D is correct. Option C, LSI, came later and led to the microprocessors of the fourth generation.

questions.question: The main electronic component used in first generation computers was
questions.explanation: Vacuum tubes and valves were the main electronic part of first generation computers. Option A, transistors, came in the second generation, and option C, integrated circuits, came in the third.

questions.question: Which of the following was a special purpose computer?
questions.explanation: The Atanasoff-Berry Computer (ABC) was built for one purpose: solving systems of linear equations, so it was a special-purpose computer. Options B and C, ENIAC and EDVAC, were general-purpose machines, so option D is also wrong.

questions.question: What was the computer invented by Atanasoff and Clifford?
questions.explanation: John Atanasoff and Clifford Berry built the Atanasoff-Berry Computer, known as the ABC. Option A, the Mark I, was built by Howard Aiken with IBM, and option C, the Z3, was built by Konrad Zuse.

questions.question: Which computer was considered the first electronic computer until 1973 when court invalidated the patent?
questions.explanation: ENIAC was widely treated as the first electronic computer until a 1973 US court case invalidated its patent and credited earlier work by Atanasoff. Option D, the ABC, is the machine that court decision favoured. Options B and C, the Mark I and Z3, were electromechanical.

questions.question: When was vacuum tube invented?
questions.explanation: Lee de Forest invented the triode vacuum tube in 1906, and this tube could amplify and switch electrical signals, which made it useful in early electronic computers. An earlier, simpler two-part tube came in 1904, but that year is not among the options. Options A, C and D, 1900, 1910 and 1880, do not match the invention of the vacuum tube.

questions.question: Computers with 80286 microprocessor is
questions.explanation: IBM's PC/AT (Advanced Technology) computers used the Intel 80286 microprocessor. Option A, the PC/XT, used the older 8088 processor. Option C, PS/2, was a later IBM line.

questions.question: The digital computer was developed primarily in
questions.explanation: Most early digital computers, such as the ABC, ENIAC, EDVAC and UNIVAC, were developed in the USA. The UK (option D) also built early machines, but the USA led the main development.

questions.question: Today's computer giant IBM was earlier known by different name which was changes in 1924. What was that name?
questions.explanation: IBM was earlier called the Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company (CTR) before it took the name International Business Machines in 1924. Options A, C and D are not its former names.

questions.question: Abacus was the first
questions.explanation: The abacus is a calculating device worked by hand with beads, and it is regarded as the earliest mechanical calculating aid. Options A and C are wrong because it has no electronic parts. Option B is wrong because it cannot store programs like a computer.

questions.question: On an abacus, the value of each bead in heaven is
questions.explanation: On an abacus, the beads above the dividing bar are called heaven beads and each one is worth 5, while the beads below the bar, the earth beads, are worth 1 each. Option A, 1, is the value of an earth bead, not a heaven bead. Options B and D, 3 and 7, are not bead values on a standard abacus.

questions.question: Which generation of computer is still under development
questions.explanation: The fifth generation, based on artificial intelligence, runs from the present into the future and is still being developed. Option A, the fourth generation, is already established. Options C and D are not standard generations.

questions.question: Which was the most popular first generation computer?
questions.explanation: The IBM 650 was the most widely used first-generation computer, built with vacuum tubes and a magnetic drum. Option B, the IBM 360, is third generation, and option C, the IBM 1130, came later as well.

questions.question: When was the world's first laptop computer introduced in the market and by whom?
questions.explanation: The Epson HX-20, released in 1981, is commonly cited as the first laptop computer. Option D, the Tandy Model 200, came later. Option C is a software company, not a laptop maker.

questions.question: From which generation operating systems were developed?
questions.explanation: Operating systems were introduced in the third generation, which let users work through keyboards and monitors instead of punched cards. In the first generation (option A) there was no operating system. In the second generation (option B) human operators still handled punched cards.

questions.question: The first firm to mass-market a microcomputer as a personal computer was
questions.explanation: Radio Shack (Tandy) mass-marketed its TRS-80 microcomputer to ordinary buyers in 1977 through its many stores. Option A, IBM, entered the personal computer market later, in 1981. Options B and D were known for larger computers.

questions.question: Why are vacuum tubes also called valves?

options.a: Because they can amplify the weak signals and make them strong
options.b: Because they can stop or allow the flow of current

questions.explanation: Vacuum tubes are called valves because, like a water valve, they can allow or block the flow of electric current. Option A, amplification, is something tubes can do, but it is not why they got the name valve.

questions.question: John Napier invented Logarithm in
questions.explanation: John Napier published his invention of logarithms in 1614. Option B, 1617, is when he described his calculating rods, known as Napier's bones, which is a different invention.

questions.question: An integrated circuit is

options.c: Much costlier than a single transistor
options.d: Fabricated on a tiny silicon chip

questions.explanation: An integrated circuit is many electronic components, such as transistors, fabricated together on a tiny silicon chip. Option A is too vague, and option C is wrong because ICs made circuits cheaper, not more costly.

questions.question: When was Pascaline invented?
questions.explanation: Blaise Pascal invented the Pascaline, a mechanical adding machine, in 1642. Option D, 1837, is when Babbage conceived the Analytical Engine. Option A, 1617, is when Napier described his calculating rods.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is valid?

options.a: Lady Augusta is the first programmer
options.b: Ada is the daughter of Lord Byron, a famous English poet
options.c: ADA is a programming language developed by US Defense

questions.explanation: Lady Ada Augusta Lovelace is called the first programmer, she was the daughter of the poet Lord Byron, and the Ada language was developed for the US Department of Defense. Since statements A, B and C are all true, option D is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first computer to use Stored Program Concept?
questions.explanation: EDSAC, completed in 1949, was the first practical computer to use the stored program concept, keeping both instructions and data in memory. Option B, ENIAC, was programmed by setting switches and cables. Option A, UNIVAC, came later.

questions.question: What is the date when Babbage conceived Analytical engine
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage conceived the Analytical Engine in 1837, a design with a processing unit (mill) and memory (store) like a modern computer. Option A, 1642, is when Pascal built his adding machine.

questions.question: What was the expected feature of fifth generation computers when Japan started FGCS?
questions.explanation: When Japan launched its Fifth Generation Computer Systems (FGCS) project, it aimed for machines using massive parallel processing to support artificial intelligence. Option A, operating systems, came in the third generation. Option C, ULSI, is a chip technology, not the project's main goal.

questions.question: When was the first electro-mechanical computer developed?
questions.explanation: The first major electro-mechanical computer, the Harvard Mark I, was completed in 1944. Option A, 1880, is before such machines existed, and option B, 1990, is far too late.

questions.question: The first machine to successfully perform a long series of arithmetic and logical operations was:
questions.explanation: The Harvard Mark I (1944) was the first machine to carry out long series of arithmetic and logical operations automatically. Option C, the Analytical Engine, was never completed. Options A and D, ENIAC and UNIVAC-1, came after it.

questions.question: IBM 1401 is
questions.explanation: The IBM 1401 belongs to the IBM 1400 family, which was built with transistors, the hallmark of second generation computers. Option A would need vacuum tubes, while option C (third generation) is the era of integrated circuits such as the IBM 360.

questions.question: Most of the first generation computers were
questions.explanation: Most early vacuum tube machines were built to solve particular kinds of problems, such as military or scientific calculations, so they are described as special purpose computers. Truly general purpose computers became common in later generations, which is why option B is not the best answer.

questions.question: Who invented Integrated Circuits?
questions.explanation: The integrated circuit was developed independently by Jack Kilby and Robert Noyce, so both of them are credited with its invention. Choosing only A or only B leaves out one of the two inventors.

questions.question: What was the main disadvantage of vacuum tubes?

options.b: They consumed a lot of electricity
options.c: They produced heat and often burned out

questions.explanation: Vacuum tubes gave off a great deal of heat and burned out frequently, making first generation computers unreliable and hard to keep running. Options A, B and D (large size, high power use, high cost) were real drawbacks too, but they largely followed from the heat and failure problem, which is the main disadvantage usually cited.

questions.question: Who invented vacuum tubes?
questions.explanation: Lee de Forest is credited with inventing the triode vacuum tube, which could amplify signals and switch currents. Options A and B, John Bardeen and William Shockley, are known for inventing the transistor, which later replaced the vacuum tube, so option D is also wrong.

questions.question: Who suggested Stored Program Concept
questions.explanation: John von Neumann proposed the stored program concept, in which both the program instructions and the data are kept in the computer's memory. Options A and B, Mauchly and Eckert, built ENIAC, and option D, Jacquard, used punched cards to control looms.

questions.question: The notable features like keyboards and monitors, which replaced punched cards and printouts, were developed in
questions.explanation: Third generation computers phased out punched cards and printouts, so for the first time users could work with the computer directly through keyboards and monitors, helped by an operating system. Options A and B, the first and second generations, still relied on punched cards for input and printouts for output. Option D, the fourth generation, kept using keyboards and monitors, but they were not first introduced there.

questions.question: Who is credited with the idea of using punch cards to control patterns in a weaving machine?
questions.explanation: Joseph Marie Jacquard used punched cards to control the patterns woven by a loom, an idea later borrowed for computers. Option B, Hollerith, used punched cards for census data processing, while Pascal and Babbage (A and C) built or designed calculating machines.

questions.question: The earliest calculating devices are
questions.explanation: The abacus, a frame of beads on rods, is one of the earliest known calculating devices. Option C, the Difference Engine, came thousands of years later in the 1800s, and option B, a clock, measures time rather than performing calculations.

questions.question: What was the first computer to perform all calculation using electronics rather than wheels, ratchets, or mechanical switches?
questions.explanation: The Atanasoff-Berry Computer (ABC) is widely credited as the first computer to do all its calculations electronically, using vacuum tubes instead of moving mechanical parts. Options A and C, the Mark I and Z3, were electromechanical machines that relied on relays and switches.

questions.question: Which of the following device was not invented by Babbage?
questions.explanation: The Pascaline was a mechanical adding machine built by Blaise Pascal in the 1600s, not by Babbage. Options B and C, the Difference Engine and the Analytical Engine, were both designed by Charles Babbage.

questions.question: The Second Generation Computer was based on
questions.explanation: Second generation computers replaced vacuum tubes with transistors, which made them smaller, faster and more reliable. Option A, vacuum tubes, defined the first generation, and option B, silicon chips, belongs to the third and fourth generations.

questions.question: IBM System/360 is
questions.explanation: The IBM System/360 was a family of large mainframe computers introduced in the third generation. Minicomputers and microcomputers (options B and C) are smaller classes that came into wide use later.

questions.question: ENIAC uses
questions.explanation: ENIAC stored and worked with numbers in decimal form, using ten-position ring counters for each digit, instead of binary. Binary-based designs such as EDVAC (option C) came later, and octal and hexadecimal (B and D) were never its number system.

questions.question: Which American computer company is called Big Blue?
questions.explanation: IBM earned the nickname Big Blue from its blue logo and its long dominance of the computer industry. Microsoft and Compaq (A and B) never carried this nickname.

questions.question: Who is the inventor of ABC Computer?
questions.explanation: The Atanasoff-Berry Computer was built by John Atanasoff together with his graduate student Clifford Berry, and its name comes from both of them. Choosing only A or only B leaves out one of the inventors.

questions.question: Find out who is not the inventor of transistors among following names
questions.explanation: Lee de Forest is known for the triode vacuum tube, not the transistor. The transistor was invented by John Bardeen, William Shockley and Walter Brattain (options A, B and C).

questions.question: The computer size was very large in
questions.explanation: First generation computers used thousands of vacuum tubes and filled whole rooms, so they were the largest in size. Every later generation (options B, C and D) became smaller as transistors and chips replaced tubes.

questions.question: IBM 7000 digital computer
questions.explanation: The IBM 7000 series, such as the IBM 7090, were transistor-based machines, which places them in the second generation. Options B and C describe much later technology, very large scale integration and semiconductor memory, which came with the third and fourth generations.

questions.question: Which of the following is first generation computer?
questions.explanation: EDSAC was an early vacuum tube computer completed in 1949, making it a first generation machine. The IBM 1401 and CDC 1604 (B and C) were transistor-based second generation computers.

questions.question: Which of the following programming language were used in first generation computers?
questions.explanation: First generation computers were programmed directly in machine language, made up of binary 0s and 1s. Option B, assembly language, came into general use with the second generation, so options B and C are not the best answers.

questions.question: Who used punched cards practically for the first time in the history of computers?
questions.explanation: Herman Hollerith was the first to use punched cards for processing data, tabulating the 1890 US census with his card machines. Option D, Jacquard, used cards to control looms rather than to process data, and option A, Babbage, only planned to use them in his designs.

questions.question: The first general purpose electronic computer in the world was
questions.explanation: ENIAC, completed in 1946, is known as the first general purpose electronic computer. EDVAC and UNIVAC (options A and B) were built later by the same designers.

questions.question: For what was the Antikythera used?
questions.explanation: The Antikythera mechanism was an ancient Greek geared device used to calculate the positions of the sun, moon and planets and to predict eclipses. Options A, B and D describe other uses that do not match what the device was designed for.

questions.question: Microprocessors can be used to make
questions.explanation: Microprocessors are used to build computers, calculators and many other digital systems, from phones to washing machines. Since options A, B and C are all correct, option D is the answer.

questions.question: Who invented Slide Rules?
questions.explanation: William Oughtred invented the slide rule in the 1620s, building on John Napier's logarithms. Option A, Napier, invented logarithms and Napier's bones, not the slide rule itself, while Leibniz and Pascal (C and D) built mechanical calculators.

questions.question: In which year was chip used inside the computer for the first time?
questions.explanation: Integrated circuit chips first appeared inside computers with the third generation in the mid-1960s, such as the IBM System/360 announced in 1964. Option B, 1975, is well into the microprocessor era, and option D, 1944, is the vacuum tube era.

questions.question: Assembly language started to be used from
questions.explanation: Assembly language came into general use with second generation computers, along with early high level languages. First generation machines (option A) were mostly programmed directly in machine language.

questions.question: Which technology is more reliable?

options.d: For reliability it does not matter. So all of above are reliable

questions.explanation: Electronic technology has no moving parts to wear out, so it is more reliable than mechanical or electro-mechanical designs. Option D is wrong because the technology used makes a big difference to reliability.

questions.question: Which of the following computer is not invented by J.P. Eckert and John Mauchly?
questions.explanation: EDSAC was built at Cambridge University in England by a team led by Maurice Wilkes, not by Eckert and Mauchly. ENIAC, EDVAC and UNIVAC (options A, B and C) all involved Eckert and Mauchly.

questions.question: When was the company named IBM?
questions.explanation: The company took the name International Business Machines (IBM) in 1924, after earlier operating as the Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company. Option A, 1914, is when Thomas Watson joined the company, not when it was renamed.

questions.question: Who invented Mark I?
questions.explanation: Howard Aiken designed the Harvard Mark I, an electromechanical computer built with IBM and completed in 1944. Options B and C, Eckert and Mauchly, built ENIAC, and option D, Atanasoff, built the ABC.

questions.question: When did arch rivals IBM and Apple Computers Inc. decide to join hands?
questions.explanation: IBM and Apple announced their alliance in 1991, working together on the PowerPC processor and related software. The other years come before this partnership was formed.

questions.question: A vacuum tube was NOT used to act like
questions.explanation: Vacuum tubes in early computers worked as amplifiers, making weak signals stronger, and as electronic switches that turned current on and off to represent 0s and 1s. A router is a networking device that directs data between networks, which has nothing to do with what a vacuum tube did. Options A and B are real jobs of a vacuum tube, so they are not the answer, and option D is wrong because C fits.

questions.question: Excessive parallel processing is related to
questions.explanation: The fifth generation is marked by large-scale parallel processing, with machines using hundreds of processors working on different parts of a single program. Earlier generations (A, B and D) mainly worked with one processor at a time.

questions.question: Second generation computers were built mainly with which technology?
questions.explanation: In the second generation, transistors replaced vacuum tubes, making computers smaller, faster, cheaper and more reliable. Vacuum tubes belong to the first generation, while integrated circuits and microprocessors mark the third and fourth generations.

questions.question: Which of the following computer implemented binary numbers, perform calculations using electronics and implemented separate computation and memory for the first time?
questions.explanation: The Atanasoff-Berry Computer (ABC) introduced binary arithmetic, electronic calculation and a separate memory from the computing unit. Options A and C, the Mark I and Z3, used electromechanical relays rather than fully electronic computation.

questions.question: Who developed a mechanical device in the 17th century that could add, subtract, multiply, divide and find square roots?
questions.explanation: Gottfried Leibniz built the Stepped Reckoner in the 17th century, a mechanical calculator that could add, subtract, multiply, divide and work out square roots. Option C, Pascal's machine, could mainly add and subtract, and option B, Babbage, worked in the 19th century.

questions.question: The first Macintosh computer was from
questions.explanation: The Apple Macintosh was a microcomputer built around a microprocessor, which places it in the fourth generation. Earlier generations (A, B and C) used vacuum tubes, transistors or early integrated circuits and had no personal microcomputers.

questions.question: Which of the following machine was not invented by Charles Babbage?
questions.explanation: Herman Hollerith built the Tabulating Machine for the 1890 US census, not Charles Babbage. Babbage designed both the Analytical Engine and the Difference Engine, so options B and C, and option D which names both of them, are all machines he did invent.

questions.question: How many numbers could ENIAC store in its internal memory
questions.explanation: ENIAC had no stored-program memory; its 20 accumulators could each hold one 10-digit number, so it could store 20 numbers internally. Options A, C and D overstate or understate this small working store.

questions.question: Which of the following is used for manufacturing chips?
questions.explanation: Chips are made from semiconductor material, mainly silicon, whose conductivity can be controlled to form transistors and circuits. A control bus, control unit and parity unit (A, B, C) are parts or functions of a computer, not manufacturing materials.

questions.question: The value of each bead in earth is
questions.explanation: On a Chinese-style abacus, each bead in the lower deck (the earth) is worth 1, while each bead in the upper deck (the heaven) is worth 5. Values like 3 or 7 (B, D) are not assigned to any bead, and 5 (C) belongs to the heaven beads.

questions.question: When did John Napier develop logarithm?
questions.explanation: John Napier published his work on logarithms in 1614. The year 1617 is linked to Napier's Bones, while 1416, 1641 and 1804 (A, C, D) are not connected to his logarithms.

questions.question: The first digital computer built with IC chips was known as
questions.explanation: The IBM System/360 is the classic example of a third-generation computer built with integrated-circuit technology. The IBM 7090 (A) was a transistor-based second-generation machine, while the Apple I (B) and VAX (D) came later, in the microprocessor and minicomputer eras.

questions.question: The first microprocessor built by the Intel corporation was called
questions.explanation: Intel's first microprocessor was the 4004, released in 1971 as a 4-bit chip. The 8008 and 8080 (A, B) were later Intel processors, and 8800 (D) is not an Intel microprocessor.

questions.question: Who invented EDSAC?
questions.explanation: EDSAC was built by Maurice Wilkes at Cambridge University and ran its first program in 1949, making it one of the first practical stored-program computers. Eckert and Mauchly (B) built ENIAC, Howard Aiken (D) built the Mark I, and von Neumann (A) described the stored-program idea.

questions.question: Why ABC computer is called so?

options.a: Because it was developed by Atanasoff and Berry
options.b: Because it was thought to be the first computer so named with first alphabets of English
options.c: Both of above are the reason to name the computer ABC

questions.explanation: The ABC is named after its builders, John Atanasoff and Clifford Berry: Atanasoff-Berry Computer. It has nothing to do with being the first computer or the first letters of the alphabet, so B and C are wrong.

questions.question: Who designed the first electronic computer - ENIAC?

options.c: J. P. Eckert and J. W. Mauchly

questions.explanation: ENIAC was designed and built by J. Presper Eckert and John W. Mauchly at the University of Pennsylvania. Von Neumann (A) is known for the stored-program idea, and Jacquard (B) invented the punched-card loom.

questions.question: IBM 1401 computer was
questions.explanation: The IBM 1401 was a transistorised second-generation mainframe widely used by businesses in the 1960s. Mini and micro computers (B, C) came later with integrated circuits and microprocessors.

questions.question: Who invented the microprocessor?
questions.explanation: Marcian 'Ted' Hoff of Intel is credited with designing the first microprocessor, the Intel 4004. Herman Goldstine (B) worked on ENIAC and Joseph Jacquard (C) invented the punched-card loom, so D is also wrong.

questions.question: MSI is the abbreviation of
questions.explanation: MSI stands for Medium Scale Integration (Integrated), meaning chips with roughly tens to hundreds of logic gates. 'System' and 'Intelligent' (B, C, D) are not part of the term.

questions.question: Which of the following is not true?

options.d: Transistors were used in radios and other electronic devices

questions.explanation: The false statement is that transistors were less reliable; in fact transistors made second-generation computers much more reliable than vacuum tubes. Being smaller, producing less heat and being used in radios (A, B, D) are all true.

questions.question: A characteristic of card systems is:

options.b: Using cards as records of transactions

questions.explanation: Punched-card systems were slow at processing, used cards as the records of transactions, and needed many data processing staff to punch and handle the cards. Since A, B and C all describe card systems, D is correct.

questions.question: Fifth generation computer is also known as
questions.explanation: Fifth-generation computers are also called Knowledge Information Processing Systems (KIPS), because they aim to process knowledge and use artificial intelligence. VLSI (B) is a chip technology linked mainly to the fourth generation, not another name for the fifth.

questions.question: Which was the computer conceived by Babbage?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine, a general-purpose mechanical computer with input, a mill for processing, a store for memory and output. Option B, the Arithmetic Machine, is linked with Blaise Pascal, not Babbage. Option C, Donald Knuth, is a computer scientist, not a machine, so option D is also wrong.

questions.question: The processing speed of first generation computers was
questions.explanation: First-generation computers built from vacuum tubes performed calculations in milliseconds. Microseconds (B) belong to the second generation, nanoseconds (C) to the third, and picoseconds (D) to much later machines.

questions.question: Which 8-bit chip was used in many TRS-80 computers?
questions.explanation: The TRS-80 microcomputers sold by Radio Shack (Models I, III and 4) used the Zilog Z-80, an 8-bit processor chip. Option A, the Z-8000, was a later 16-bit Zilog chip, and option B, the Intel 8086, is a 16-bit chip that powered IBM-type PCs rather than the TRS-80. Option C, Z-8808, is not a real processor name.

questions.question: The word Abacus is derived from Abax, a word from
questions.explanation: Abax is a Greek word meaning a board or calculating table, and it gave Latin the word abacus. Latin (A) borrowed the word from Greek, and Sanskrit and Ancient Egyptian (C, D) are not connected to it.

questions.question: In latest generation computers, the instructions are executed
questions.explanation: Modern computers execute instructions both sequentially and in parallel, using multiple processors or cores to work on different parts of a program at once. Parallel only or sequential only (A, B) each leave out half of the picture.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of fifth generation computer?
questions.explanation: PIM/m is a parallel inference machine built under Japan's Fifth Generation Computer project, so it is a fifth-generation computer. The IBM 1401 (C) is second generation and the ICL 2950 (B) is an older mainframe.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a third generation computer?
questions.explanation: The IBM 1401 used transistors, so it is a second-generation computer. The IBM 360, PDP-8 and HP 2115 (A, C, D) belong to the third generation.

questions.question: Mark I is also known as
questions.explanation: The Harvard Mark I, built by Howard Aiken with IBM, is also called the Automatic Sequence Controlled Calculator (ASCC). The other options (A, B, C) change 'Automatic' or 'Calculator', so they are wrong.

questions.question: Who built the first Mechanical Calculator
questions.explanation: Blaise Pascal built the Pascaline in 1642, a mechanical calculator that could add and subtract. Jacquard (A) built the punched-card loom, Mauchly (B) co-built ENIAC, and Aiken (D) built the electromechanical Mark I.

questions.question: Which of the following generation computers had expensive operation cost?
questions.explanation: First-generation computers were very expensive to run because thousands of vacuum tubes used a lot of electricity, produced great heat and needed constant maintenance. Later generations (B, C, D) became cheaper, smaller and more reliable.

questions.question: The lower deck of an abacus is known as
questions.explanation: On an abacus the lower deck is called the earth and the upper deck is called the heaven. 'Sky' and 'floor' (B, D) are not the names used, and heaven (A) is the upper deck.

questions.question: The IBM 1401 computer belonged to which generation?
questions.explanation: The IBM 1401 used transistors, so it belongs to the second generation of computers. First-generation machines (A) used vacuum tubes, and third- and fourth-generation machines (C, D) used integrated circuits and microprocessors.

questions.question: The Third Generation Computer was made with ____.
questions.explanation: Third-generation computers were built with integrated circuits (ICs), which put many transistors on one silicon chip. Vacuum tubes (A) belong to the first generation, discrete components (B) to the second, and bio-chips (D) to future machines.

questions.question: Who built the world's first electronic calculator using telephone relays, light bulbs and batteries?
questions.explanation: George Stibitz of Bell Labs built a relay-based adding circuit, the Model K, using telephone relays, light bulbs and batteries in 1937. Claude Shannon (A) wrote on switching theory, Konrad Zuse (B) built the Z-series machines, and Howard Aiken (D) built the Mark I.

questions.question: In the IBM PC-At, what do the words AT stand for
questions.explanation: In IBM PC-AT, AT stands for Advanced Technology, the name IBM gave the 1984 model built on the Intel 80286. 'Additional Terminals', 'Applied technology' and 'Advanced terminology' (A, C, D) are not what AT means.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of fifth generation computers?
questions.explanation: Fifth-generation computers aim to use natural language, artificial intelligence and advanced technologies such as bio-chips. Since A, B and C are all features linked with this generation, D is correct.

questions.question: Charles Babbage was awarded by Royal Society for his

options.d: His concept of input, mill, output and storage

questions.explanation: Babbage's Difference Engine, a machine for calculating mathematical tables, earned him recognition and official support in the 1820s. The Analytical Engine (B) and his concept of input, mill, store and output (D) came later and were never completed in his lifetime.

questions.question: The operating speed of third generation computer was
questions.explanation: Third-generation computers, built with integrated circuits, operated in nanoseconds (billionths of a second). Milliseconds (A) belong to the first generation and microseconds (B) to the second.

questions.question: Which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: The Harvard Mark I was a huge machine about 51 feet long, so none of the lengths given is correct. It stood about 8 feet high and was about 2 feet deep, which is why options A and B can look familiar, but those are its height and depth, not its length. Option C, 40 feet, is still too short.

questions.question: The first electronic general purpose digital computer built by Eckert and Mauchly called ENIAC did not work on the stored program concept. How many numbers could it store in its internal memory?
questions.explanation: ENIAC could hold only 20 numbers in its internal memory, one in each of its 20 accumulators, with each number up to 10 decimal digits. The other values (A, C, D) do not match its accumulator count.

questions.question: What was the name of the first commercially available microprocessor chip?
questions.explanation: The Intel 4004, released in 1971, was the first commercially available microprocessor chip. The other names (A, B, D) are not real early microprocessors.

questions.question: When did IBM introduce the 80286 based PC/AT?
questions.explanation: IBM introduced the PC/AT, based on the Intel 80286 processor, in 1984. 1982 (A) is too early for that chip in a PC, and 1985 and 1989 (C, D) are too late.

questions.question: The silicon chips used for data processing are called
questions.explanation: Microprocessors are the silicon chips that do data processing, since each contains a CPU on a single chip. RAM, ROM and PROM chips (A, B, D) are memory chips that store data rather than process it.

questions.question: Which computers used operating systems by Microsoft?
questions.explanation: Microsoft's operating systems, from MS-DOS to Windows, were made for IBM PCs and IBM-compatible computers. Apple Macintosh computers (B) used Apple's own operating system, so D is the correct combination.

questions.question: One of the main feature that distinguish microprocessors from micro-computer is

options.a: Words are usually large in microprocessors
options.c: Microprocessor does not contain I/O device
options.d: Microprocessors always have more memory than microcomputers

questions.explanation: A microprocessor is just the CPU on a single chip, while a microcomputer is a complete computer built around it, with memory and input/output devices. Word size (A, B) is not what separates them, and D is wrong because a microprocessor on its own is only the processor, not a computer with its own memory.

questions.question: Computers built just before the First Generation of computers were:
questions.explanation: The machines built just before the first generation, such as the Harvard Mark I, used electrical relays together with moving mechanical parts, so they were electro-mechanical. Fully electronic machines using vacuum tubes (A) are what define the first generation itself, and optical computers (C) were never part of this history.

questions.question: Artificial Intelligence is associated with which generation?
questions.explanation: Artificial intelligence is the defining feature of the fifth generation of computers, which aim to reason, learn and make decisions. First and second generations (A, B) used vacuum tubes and transistors, and a 'sixth generation' (D) is not one of the standard five.

questions.question: How was the generation of computer classified?

options.a: by the device used in memory & processor
options.c: by the model of the computer

questions.explanation: Computer generations are classified by the main electronic device used in the processor and memory: vacuum tubes, transistors, ICs, microprocessors and AI technology. Speed, model and accuracy (B, C, D) improved with each generation but are not what defines it.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a feature of first generation computers

options.a: They used vacuum tubes or valves as main electronic component
options.b: They consumed lots of electricity and produced excessive heat
options.c: They were programmed in high-level languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL

questions.explanation: First-generation computers were programmed in low-level machine language; high-level languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL came in with the second generation. That makes C the statement that is not a first-generation feature. Using vacuum tubes (A) and using lots of electricity while producing much heat (B) are true first-generation features, so D is wrong.

questions.question: Who invented Analytical engine?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine, the forerunner of the modern computer. Pascal (A) built the Pascaline, Boole (B) developed Boolean algebra, and Hollerith (D) built the tabulating machine.

questions.question: The Stepped Reckoner was invented by
questions.explanation: The Stepped Reckoner was a mechanical calculator built by the German mathematician Gottfried Leibniz, and it could add, subtract, multiply and divide. Option D, Blaise Pascal, built the earlier Pascaline, while John Napier (A) is known for Napier's bones and logarithms, and William Oughtred (B) for the slide rule.

questions.question: In a punched card system, data is processed by a

options.a: Keypunch machine, sorter and posting machine
options.b: Accounting machine, posting machine, and billing machine
options.c: Sorter, posting machine, and billing machine
options.d: Accounting machine, keypunch machine and sorter

questions.explanation: A classic punched card system used a keypunch machine to punch data onto cards, a sorter to arrange the cards in the needed order, and an accounting machine (tabulator) to total and print results. Options A, B and C include posting and billing machines, which were not the core units for processing punched card data.

questions.question: A set of rods where numbers were carved and used for multiplication and division aids is known as
questions.explanation: Napier's bones were a set of numbered rods invented by John Napier to make multiplication and division easier. The Pascaline (A) and Stepped Reckoner (C) were geared mechanical calculators, and the slide rule (D) uses sliding logarithmic scales rather than carved rods.

questions.question: Punched cards were first introduced by
questions.explanation: Joseph Marie Jacquard introduced punched cards in the early 1800s to control the patterns on his weaving loom, long before they were used for computing. Herman Hollerith (D) later adapted punched cards for data processing in the 1890 US census, and James Powers (A) improved on Hollerith's machines. Pascal (B) built a mechanical calculator, not punched cards.

questions.question: The contribution of Konrad Zuse was long ignored because

options.b: his computers were very complicated and it took time for the people to recognize its power
options.c: of political reasons. He was German.

questions.explanation: Konrad Zuse built his early computers in Germany around the time of the Second World War, and for political reasons, because he was German at a time of war, his work was long overlooked in Britain and America. That makes C the answer. Secrecy (A) and complexity (B) are not the reasons usually given, so D is wrong too.

questions.question: Which of the following is related to fifth generation computers?
questions.explanation: Fifth generation computers are built around artificial intelligence and knowledge information processing systems that can reason and make decisions. VLSI (B) is the chip technology that defines the fourth generation, so C and D are wrong.

questions.question: MSI stands for
questions.explanation: MSI stands for Medium Scale Integration (Medium Scale Integrated circuits), a chip with tens to hundreds of components, used in third generation computers. The other options swap in wrong words such as System or Intelligent, which are not part of the term.

questions.question: What was the nick name of the computer used by the Americans in 1952 for their H-bomb project?
questions.explanation: MANIAC (Mathematical Analyzer, Numerical Integrator and Computer) was built at Los Alamos and completed in 1952, where it was used for hydrogen bomb calculations. ENIAC (A) was the earlier wartime machine, EDSAC (B) was British, and UNIVAC (D) was a commercial computer.
