questions.explanation: The blocking factor is the number of logical records grouped into one block on tape. Grouping records this way reduces the gaps between blocks and saves space; the other options (A, B, D) are not standard terms for this.

questions.question: During the fetch step, which register finally holds the instruction fetched from the memory location pointed to by the program counter (PC), ready to be decoded?
questions.explanation: In the fetch step, the instruction stored at the address held in the PC is brought from memory and placed in the instruction register (IR), where the control unit decodes it. The memory data register (B) only passes the word along on its way from memory, so it is not where the instruction is held for decoding. The memory address register (A) holds an address, not the instruction, and the PC (D) holds the address of the next instruction.

questions.question: Latency time is

options.a: Time to spin the needed data under head
options.b: Time to spin the needed data under track
options.c: Time to spin data under sector

questions.explanation: Latency (rotational delay) is the time it takes for the disk to spin the needed data under the read/write head. The head, not the track or sector, is what reads the data, so B and C are not the correct definition.

questions.question: Cursor is a
questions.explanation: A cursor is the thin blinking line (or marker) on the screen that shows where the next character you type will appear. A pixel (A) is a single dot of the display, and a pointing device (C) is hardware such as a mouse.

questions.question: Which device is used to backup the data?
questions.explanation: Floppy disks, tapes and network drives can all hold copies of data for backup. Since A, B and C are all used for backup, D is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following printers are you sure will not to use if your objective is to print on multi carbon forms?
questions.explanation: A laser printer is a non-impact printer, so it cannot press through carbon layers to print copies on multi-part forms. Daisy wheel, dot matrix and thimble printers (A, B, D) are impact printers that strike the paper and can print carbon copies.

questions.question: A normal CD-ROM usually can store up to data?
questions.explanation: A standard CD-ROM holds roughly 650-700 MB of data, so 680 MB is the correct size. Kilobytes and bytes (A, B) are far too small, and gigabytes (D) are far too large for a CD.

questions.question: Offline device is

options.a: A device which is not connected to CPU
options.b: A device which is connected to CPU

questions.explanation: An offline device is one not connected to or controlled by the CPU at that moment. A device connected to the CPU (B) is online, and direct access storage or I/O devices (C, D) can be online or offline.

questions.question: Which one of the following input device is user- programmable?
questions.explanation: An intelligent terminal has its own processor and memory, so the user can program it to do some processing locally. Dumb terminals (A) can only send and display data, and smart terminals and VDTs (B, C) have limited, non-programmable functions.

questions.question: Current SIMMs have either ____ pins.
questions.explanation: SIMM memory modules came in two standard sizes, 30-pin and 72-pin. The other pairs of numbers (options A, B and C) are not SIMM pin counts, even though 72 appears in option C alongside the wrong partner, 28.

questions.question: Dot-matrix is a type of
questions.explanation: Dot-matrix is a type of impact printer that forms characters from a grid of tiny dots made by pins striking an ink ribbon. It is not a tape, disk or bus (A, C, D).

questions.question: Which of the following is not a part of the processor (CPU)?
questions.explanation: A processor contains the ALU, the control unit and registers, but main memory is a separate component outside the CPU. So memory (C) is the one not contained in the processor, while A, B and D are all parts of it.

questions.question: Which of the following are the two main components of the CPU?
questions.explanation: The two main parts of the CPU are the control unit, which directs operations, and the arithmetic logic unit (ALU), which does calculations and comparisons. Main memory and the bus (B, D) are outside the CPU, and registers (A) are small storage areas rather than one of the two main units.

questions.question: What is the name of the computer terminal which gives paper printout?
questions.explanation: A hard copy terminal produces printed paper output that you can hold. A display screen or soft copy terminal (A, B) shows output only on screen, and a plotter (D) draws graphics rather than acting as a terminal.

questions.question: The personnel who deals with the computer and its management put together are called
questions.explanation: Humanware (also called liveware) means the people who use, operate and manage the computer. Software (A) is programs, firmware (C) is software stored in ROM, and hardware (D) is the physical equipment.

questions.question: Which of the following is input device?
questions.explanation: A scanner is an input device: it captures images or documents and sends them into the computer. Speakers, monitors and projectors (B, C, D) are output devices.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct acronym of VGA?
questions.explanation: VGA stands for Video Graphics Array, a display standard introduced by IBM. 'Visual', 'Volatile' and 'Adapter' (B, C, D) are not part of the correct expansion.

questions.question: A song being played on computer speaker is
questions.explanation: Sound from a speaker is soft output because it is temporary and cannot be held like paper. Hard output (A) is permanent output such as a printout, so a song is not hard output.

questions.question: What is the number of read-write heads in the drive for a 9-track magnetic tape?
questions.explanation: A 9-track tape records 9 parallel tracks (8 data bits plus a parity bit), so the drive needs one read-write head per track, 9 in all. 16, 18 and 27 (B, C, D) do not match the number of tracks.

questions.question: Which of the following will happen when data is entered into a memory location?

options.a: It will add to the content of the location
options.b: It will change the address of the memory location
options.c: It will erase the previous content
options.d: It will not be fruitful if there is already some data at the location

questions.explanation: Writing data into a memory location replaces (erases) whatever was stored there before. It does not add to the old contents (A) or change the location's address (B), and it works whether or not the location already held data (D).

questions.question: Which device is used as the standard pointing device in a Graphical User Environment?
questions.explanation: The mouse is the standard pointing device in a graphical user interface, used to move the pointer and click on icons and menus. A keyboard (A) is mainly for typing, while joysticks and trackballs (C, D) are less common alternatives.

questions.question: Pick the one that is used for logical operations or comparisons such as less than equal to or greater than.
questions.explanation: The arithmetic logic unit (ALU) carries out logical operations and comparisons such as less than, equal to and greater than, as well as arithmetic. The control unit (B) directs and coordinates operations but does not perform the comparisons itself.

questions.question: Which of the following have the fastest access time?
questions.explanation: Semiconductor memories such as RAM and cache have the fastest access times because they have no moving parts and work at electronic speed. Magnetic disks, tapes and compact disks (B, C, D) need mechanical movement, so they are much slower.

questions.question: How many types of storage loops exists in magnetic bubble memory
questions.explanation: Magnetic bubble memory uses two types of storage loops: major loops and minor loops. Data is stored in the minor loops and moved through the major loop for reading and writing, so 4, 8 and 16 (A, B, C) are wrong.

questions.question: Which of the following is a way to access secondary memory?
questions.explanation: Random access (also called direct access) means the computer can go straight to any location on the storage device, as it does on a hard disk. The other main way to reach secondary storage is sequential access, as on magnetic tape. 'Action method', 'transfer method' and 'density method' (options B, C and D) are not storage access methods at all.

questions.question: Which of the following storage media can only be read, so that its contents cannot be erased or modified by the user?
questions.explanation: CD-ROM means Compact Disc Read-Only Memory: its data is recorded at manufacture, so a user can read it but cannot erase or change it. Floppy disks, hard disks and tape (A, B, C) are magnetic media that can be erased and rewritten many times.

questions.question: Which is an item of storage medium in the form of circular plate?
questions.explanation: A disk is a storage medium in the shape of a flat circular plate, coated so it can store data magnetically or optically. The CPU, printer and ALU (B, C, D) are processing or output hardware, not storage media.

questions.question: Daisy wheel printer is a type of
questions.explanation: A daisy wheel printer is an impact printer: a spinning wheel of characters strikes an inked ribbon against the paper. It is not a matrix printer (A), since it prints fully formed characters, and it is not a laser printer (C).

questions.question: The two basic types of record access methods are:
questions.explanation: Records can be accessed either sequentially (one after another from the start) or randomly (directly, in any order). Indexed (B) is a way of organizing files that supports these methods, while immediate, online and real time (C, D) are not access methods.

questions.question: One of a class of storage devices that can access storage locations in any order is
questions.explanation: DASD stands for Direct Access Storage Device, a group of storage devices such as hard disks that can jump straight to any storage location in any order. DTE (option A) and DCE (option D) are data communication equipment terms, and DDE (option C) is a way for programs to exchange data, so none of them is a storage device.

questions.question: The actual execution of instructions happens in
questions.explanation: Instructions are actually carried out in the ALU, which performs the arithmetic and logic operations. The control unit (B) fetches, decodes and directs instructions but does not perform the calculations, and memory (C) only stores instructions and data.

questions.question: Floppy disks are available in
questions.explanation: Floppy disks were made in several formats, including single-sided single-density and single-sided double-density. Since both A and B were available, C is correct.

questions.question: As compared to the secondary memory, the primary memory of a computer is
questions.explanation: Primary memory is much faster than secondary memory, which is why the CPU works directly with it. It is smaller and more expensive (A, B are wrong), and secondary storage is the slower one (D is wrong).

questions.question: Which of the following memories has the shortest access times?
questions.explanation: Cache memory is a small, very fast memory placed close to (or inside) the CPU, so it has the shortest access time. RAM (D) is slower than cache, and magnetic bubble and core memories (B, C) are older and much slower.

questions.question: A smart or intelligent device is so called because it contains within it a
questions.explanation: A device is called smart or intelligent because it has a microprocessor built into it, a CPU on a single chip that lets it process data and follow programmed instructions. A sensor (option D) only detects things like heat or movement and cannot make decisions by itself. 'Programmable' (option C) describes a feature, not a part inside the device, and a full computer (option A) is more than such devices contain.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a primary storage device?
questions.explanation: Magnetic tape, magnetic disk and optical disk are all secondary (auxiliary) storage devices, not primary memory. Primary storage means RAM and ROM, so all three options are correct and D is the answer.

questions.question: Circular division of disks to store and retrieve data are known as
questions.explanation: Tracks are the circular rings on a disk surface where data is stored and retrieved. Sectors (B) are pie-shaped divisions of each track, while cycles and rings (C, D) are not the standard term.

questions.question: The latest PC keyboards use a circuit that senses key movement by the change in its capacitance. Such a keyboard is called a
questions.explanation: A capacitance (capacitive) keyboard detects a key press by sensing the change in capacitance as a key moves, instead of relying on metal contacts touching. A mechanical keyboard (option B) uses physical switches under each key. QWERTY and Dvorak (options C and D) are names of key layouts, not ways of sensing key presses.

questions.question: While inserting a diskette into the diskette drive of a PC, the diskette's label side should face
questions.explanation: A diskette is inserted with its label side facing up, with the metal shutter end going into the drive first. East, North and South (options A to C) are compass directions and have nothing to do with how a disk sits in a drive.

questions.question: What is a light pen?
questions.explanation: A light pen is a pen-shaped pointer with a light-sensitive tip that detects light from the screen, so it is classed as an optical input device. It is not an output device (D), because it sends position information into the computer rather than displaying results. It has no mechanical moving parts doing the sensing, so A does not fit.

questions.question: In order to play and hear sound on a computer, one needs:
questions.explanation: To play and hear sound, a computer needs a sound card to turn digital audio into an audio signal and speakers (or headphones) to produce the sound. A microphone (B) is for recording sound, not hearing it, so it is not required for playback.

questions.question: Which of the following devices can be used to directly image printed text?
questions.explanation: OCR (Optical Character Recognition) scans printed text and converts the characters into text the computer can edit. OMR (B) only detects marks such as shaded bubbles on answer sheets, and MICR (C) reads special magnetic-ink characters like those on cheques, so D is wrong.

questions.question: Seek time is

options.a: time to position the head over proper track
options.b: time to position the head over proper sector
options.c: time to transfer data from the disk to main memory

questions.explanation: Seek time is the time a disk drive takes to move its read/write head to the correct track. Waiting for the right sector to spin under the head (B) is a different delay called rotational latency, and moving the data into memory (C) is called transfer time.

questions.question: Tape speed is measured in
questions.explanation: Magnetic tape speed is traditionally measured in inches per second (ips). Feet, metres and centimetres per second (A, C and D) are not the standard units used for tape drives.

questions.question: Which computer support co-processors?
questions.explanation: Both the IBM PC XT and the IBM PC AT had a socket for a maths co-processor: the XT took the 8087 and the AT took the 80287. Since both support co-processors, D is correct; choosing only the AT (B) ignores the XT's co-processor socket.

questions.question: A floppy disk contains
questions.explanation: A floppy disk's surface is divided into circular tracks, and each track is further divided into sectors. Having only tracks (A) or only sectors (B) would not let the drive locate data, so both are needed.

questions.question: The capacity of 3.5 inch floppy disk is
questions.explanation: The standard high-density 3.5 inch floppy disk holds 1.44 MB. Options B and C say GB, which is about a thousand times too large, and 1.40 MB (A) is not the standard figure.

questions.question: The system unit of a personal computer typically contains all of the following except:
questions.explanation: The system unit normally houses the microprocessor, the disk controller and the serial interface, because these are core parts of the computer. A modem is a communication device that is often external or an optional add-on, so it is the one not typically found in every system unit.

questions.question: The process of starting or restarting a computer system by loading instructions from a secondary storage device into the computer memory is called
questions.explanation: Booting is the process of starting or restarting a computer by loading the operating system from storage into memory. Duping (A), padding (C) and CPS (D) are not terms for starting a computer.

questions.question: A/n ____ Device is any device that provides information, which is sent to the CPU
questions.explanation: An input device, such as a keyboard or mouse, supplies data and instructions that are sent to the CPU for processing. An output device (B) does the reverse, showing results from the computer, while the CPU (C) and memory (D) are not devices that feed information to the CPU.

questions.question: Which is the type of memory for information that does not change on your computer?
questions.explanation: ROM (Read Only Memory) holds instructions that do not change, such as the start-up program, and keeps them even when power is off. RAM (A) is temporary working memory whose contents change constantly and are lost when the computer is switched off.

questions.question: Which of the following registers is used to keep track of address of the memory location where the next instruction is located?
questions.explanation: The program counter holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched. The memory address register (A) holds whichever address is being accessed right now, and the instruction register (C) holds the instruction currently being carried out.

questions.question: Which computer memory is used for storing programs and data currently being processed by the CPU?
questions.explanation: Internal memory, also called main or primary memory (RAM), holds the programs and data the CPU is working on right now. Mass memory (A) is secondary storage such as hard disks, and PROM (D) is a type of read-only memory for fixed instructions.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an output device?
questions.explanation: A scanner is an input device: it reads printed pages or pictures into the computer, so it is not an output device. Printers (B) and flat screens (C) are output devices, and a touch screen (D) is both input and output because it shows images as well as accepting touch.

questions.question: Personal computers used a number of chips mounted on a main circuit board. What is the common name for such boards?
questions.explanation: The motherboard is the main circuit board that holds the CPU, memory chips and connectors for other parts. A daughterboard (A) is a smaller add-on board that plugs into the motherboard, and father board and child board (C, D) are not standard terms.

questions.question: ______ is not a peripheral unit
questions.explanation: RAM is part of the computer's main memory inside the system unit, so it is not a peripheral. A joystick (A), keyboard (B), card reader (C) and mouse (D) are all peripheral devices that connect to the computer to handle input.

questions.question: The two logical units that makes up the CPU of a computer are

options.d: Arithmetic Logic Unit and Control Unit

questions.explanation: The CPU is made up of the Arithmetic Logic Unit, which does calculations and comparisons, and the Control Unit, which directs the operations. Main memory (C) and RAM (E) work closely with the CPU but are separate units, and input and output devices (A) are outside it.

questions.question: Which of the following is used as input device for the computer?
questions.explanation: A light pen is an input device used to point at or draw on the screen. A TV (B), VDU or monitor (C) and printer (D) are output devices, and a hard disk (A) is a storage device.

questions.question: The brain of the computer is also known as?
questions.explanation: The CPU is called the brain of the computer because it carries out instructions and controls all the other parts. The keyboard (A), joystick (C) and mouse (E) are input devices, and the monitor (B) is an output device.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an integral part of a computer?
questions.explanation: A UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) is an extra device that keeps power flowing during outages; the computer can work without it, so it is not an integral part. The motherboard (A), CPU (C), monitor (E) and mouse (B) are standard parts of a computer system.

questions.question: When you save a file, it is permanently saved on the _____
questions.explanation: When you save a file, it is stored permanently on the hard drive, a secondary storage device that keeps data even when the power is off. RAM (D) only holds data temporarily and loses it at shutdown, and the CPU (A) processes data but does not store files.

questions.question: What part of the CPU performs arithmetic and logical operations
questions.explanation: The ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) performs calculations such as addition and logical operations such as comparisons. The CU (A) directs and coordinates operations but does not do the calculations, and RAM (C) is memory.

questions.question: What does the acronym CPU stand for?
questions.explanation: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit, the part of the computer that carries out instructions. The other options use wrong words such as Computational, Core or Utility.

questions.question: The main difference between hardware and software is:

options.a: Hardware is tangible, software is intangible
options.b: Software is physical, hardware is virtual
options.c: Hardware costs more than software typically

questions.explanation: Hardware is the physical, tangible part of a computer you can touch, while software is the set of instructions and has no physical form. Option B has it backwards, and C and D are not the basic difference between them.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary component of a computer system?
questions.explanation: Memory is one of the core parts of every computer system, because it holds data and instructions for the CPU. Network connections (A), printers (C) and scanners (D) are optional extras or peripherals that a computer can work without.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of a computer system?
questions.explanation: A computer system is made of hardware, software and the people who use it, and it works on data, so A, B and C are all part of it. The Internet is an outside network a computer can connect to, but a computer system works without it.

questions.question: The CPU is often referred to as the:

options.a: Core processing hub of the system

questions.explanation: The CPU is the central processing hub, often called the brain of the computer, because it carries out instructions and controls the other parts. It is not permanent storage (B), and it is not an input (D) or output (C) device.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of primary memory?
questions.explanation: RAM is primary memory: the CPU uses it directly to hold the data and programs in use right now. External hard drives (A), optical discs (C) and flash drives (D) are secondary storage.

questions.question: The function of the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) is to:
questions.explanation: The ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) carries out arithmetic, such as adding and subtracting, and logical operations, such as comparing values. It does not store data (A) or manage input and output devices (C, D).

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of secondary storage?
questions.explanation: A hard disk is secondary storage because it keeps data long-term, even when the power is off. RAM (A), ROM (B) and cache (D) are all kinds of primary memory that work directly with the CPU.

questions.question: The motherboard is:
questions.explanation: The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects the CPU, memory, storage and other parts so they can communicate. It is hardware, not a program (A), and it is not a storage device (C) or a screen (D).

questions.question: Which component of a computer system is responsible for temporary storage?
questions.explanation: RAM provides temporary storage for the data and programs in use, and its contents disappear when the computer is switched off. The hard drive (A) stores data permanently, and the display (C) and printer (D) are output devices.

questions.question: The control unit of the CPU is responsible for:

options.b: Managing data flow within the system

questions.explanation: The control unit directs and coordinates the computer's operations, managing the flow of data and instructions between the CPU, memory and input/output devices. Doing the calculations (A) is the ALU's job, and holding data (C) is the job of memory and registers.

questions.question: Which of the following is an output device?
questions.explanation: A monitor is an output device because it displays the results of processing. The keyboard (A), mouse (B) and scanner (D) are input devices that send data into the computer.

questions.question: The power supply unit (PSU) in a computer system:
questions.explanation: The power supply unit converts AC mains electricity into the lower DC voltages that the computer's parts need. It does not store data (A), do calculations (C) or display information (D).

questions.question: ROM stands for:
questions.explanation: ROM stands for Read-Only Memory, which holds fixed instructions such as the start-up program and keeps them when the power is off. The other options use wrong words such as Random, Output or Only.

questions.question: Central processing unit or processor, main memory and peripheral units are ____ components.
questions.explanation: The CPU, main memory and peripheral units are physical parts you can touch, so they are hardware components. Software (option E) is the programs, firmware (option A) is software stored in ROM, and peopleware (option C) is the human users. Middleware (option B) is software that links other programs.

questions.question: Special storage memory used by the control unit is called ____.
questions.explanation: Registers are small, very fast storage locations inside the CPU, and the control unit uses them to hold the current instruction, addresses and data while it works. The accumulator (option A) is just one particular register, so 'registers' is the general answer. Hard disks (option B) are secondary storage, and the BIOS (option D) is start-up firmware in ROM.

questions.question: Which of these is stored in Read-Only-Memory?
questions.explanation: ROM holds firmware: permanent instructions such as the BIOS and bootstrap loader, written in by the manufacturer and kept even when power is off. Hardware (option C) is the physical chip itself, not what is stored in it. Ordinary software (option E) and user data are kept on disk and loaded into RAM, not burned into ROM.

questions.question: The difference between semiconductor memory and auxiliary storage devices is that ____.

options.a: auxiliary storage devices are faster and less expensive while semiconductor memory are opposite
options.b: auxiliary storage devices are slower and less expensive while semiconductor memory are opposite
options.c: semiconductor memory are slower, volatile and more expensive while Auxiliary storage are opposite
options.d: semiconductor memory are faster, volatile and more expensive while Auxiliary storage are opposite
options.e: semiconductor memory are slower, not volatile and more expensive while Auxiliary storage are opposite

questions.explanation: Semiconductor memory (main memory such as RAM) is faster than disks, costs more per byte and is volatile, meaning it loses its contents when power goes off. Auxiliary storage such as a hard disk is the opposite: slower, cheaper and non-volatile. Options A, B, C and E each get at least one of these facts the wrong way round.

questions.question: One major disadvantage of the CD-ROM and WORM (Write once/ read many) is that

options.a: Information is not easily erasable or written over
options.b: Information is not permanently stored on them

questions.explanation: CD-ROM and WORM discs can be written only once, so information on them cannot easily be erased or written over. This makes them unsuitable when data needs updating. In fact the data is stored very permanently and is easy to read, so options B, D and E describe the opposite of these discs, and option C is not a real problem.

questions.question: Which of these is not an example of floppy disks?
questions.explanation: Floppy disks came in three common sizes: 8 inch, 5 1/4 inch and 3 1/2 inch. A 3 1/4 inch floppy disk was never a standard size, so option D is the one that is not an example. Options A, B and C are all real floppy disk sizes.

questions.question: ____ has the ALU and the CU as its components.
questions.explanation: The Central Processing Unit (CPU) is made up of the Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU), which does calculations and comparisons, and the Control Unit (CU), which coordinates everything. Memory (option D) and the storage, input and output devices (options A, B and C) are separate parts of the computer system.

questions.question: The scanner is an example of ____.
questions.explanation: A scanner reads printed documents or pictures and turns them into digital data that the computer can use, so it is an input device. Output devices (option B) such as printers and monitors do the reverse, presenting results to the user. A scanner does not store data or process it.

questions.question: The magnetic tape is best described as a(n) ____.
questions.explanation: Magnetic tape stores large amounts of data permanently, usually for backups and archives, so it is best described as a storage device. Data on tape is read in order (sequentially), and it is secondary storage, not main memory (option D). It is not mainly used to type data in or show results (options A and B).

questions.question: The dot matrix printer is an example of ____.
questions.explanation: A dot matrix printer produces printed results on paper by striking an inked ribbon with tiny pins, so it is an output device. Input devices (option A) such as keyboards and scanners send data into the computer rather than presenting results. A printer does not store or process data.

questions.question: Which of these has its speed measured in gigahertz?
questions.explanation: The speed of a CPU is measured by its clock speed, given in hertz, and modern processors run at several gigahertz (billions of cycles per second). Memory and storage (options C and D) are mainly described by capacity in bytes. Input and output devices are not rated in gigahertz.

questions.question: Blu-ray is a(n) ____.
questions.explanation: Blu-ray is an optical disc format, like CD and DVD but with much larger capacity, used to store data and high-definition video. That makes it a storage device. It is not main memory (option D), and it does not do processing like the CPU (option E).

questions.question: A computer system can be defined as a data processing machine that is capable of storing data, processing data and giving output based on the ____ given to it by the ____
questions.explanation: A computer stores and processes data and produces output according to the logic (the program instructions) given to it by the user. The computer does not decide what to do on its own. The user supplies the instructions, so options A, B and C either name the wrong giver of instructions or use the wrong first word.

questions.question: Microphone is an example of an
questions.explanation: A microphone captures sound and sends it into the computer as data, so it is an input device. Output devices (option A) such as speakers and monitors present results to the user, and storage devices (option C) keep data. A microphone does neither.

questions.question: CRT is an acronym for
questions.explanation: CRT stands for Cathode Ray Tube, the older bulky screen technology where a beam of electrons is fired at a phosphor screen to produce the picture. 'Race', 'rounded' and 'raise' (options A, B and C) are misspellings of 'ray' and are not the correct expansion.

questions.question: The users of a computer system can be one of the following
questions.explanation: A computer system can be used by a human being or by another machine, for example another computer sending it data or instructions. Software and hardware (B) are parts of the system itself, not its users, and printers, keyboards and motherboards (D and E) are hardware devices.

questions.question: The part of the computer that can be physically touched is called?
questions.explanation: Hardware is the general name for all the physical parts of a computer that you can touch. The monitor, keyboard, mouse and motherboard (A, B, D, E) are each examples of hardware, but the question asks for the name of the whole category.

questions.question: The main memory of the computer is the
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is the computer's main working memory, holding the operating system, programs and data currently in use. ROM (B) is also part of primary memory, but it is a small permanent store of start-up instructions rather than the main working area. Flash drives, floppy drives and hard disks (C, D, E) are secondary storage.

questions.question:
[Use the options below to answer Questions 73 to 80: a Input Device; b Output Device; c Storage Device; d Memory; e Central Processing Unit]
Its speed is measured in gigahertz.
questions.explanation: Processor speed, or clock speed, is measured in gigahertz (GHz), meaning billions of cycles per second. Memory and storage (D and C) are measured mainly by capacity in bytes, such as GB.

questions.question:
[Use the options below to answer Questions 73 to 80: a Input Device; b Output Device; c Storage Device; d Memory; e Central Processing Unit]
Blu-ray is a(n) ______.
questions.explanation: A Blu-ray disc is an optical disc used to store large amounts of data such as high-definition video, so it is a storage device. It is not main memory (D), because the CPU does not work directly from it.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is true about control unit?.

options.a: It obtains the address to be obeyed from the input device
options.b: It decodes the instructions into high level language
options.d: It includes the program counter, the instruction register and the decoder

questions.explanation: The control unit fetches each instruction, then increments the program counter so it points to the next one. It works with the program counter, the instruction register and the instruction decoder to carry instructions out. Option A is wrong because instruction addresses come from memory, not the input device, and B is wrong because instructions are decoded into control signals, not into a high-level language.

questions.question: You have to ______ a diskette if you need to lock it against accidental erasure
questions.explanation: Write-protecting a diskette (sliding its small tab) stops anything new being written to it or erased from it, so its contents are safe. Formatting (A) does the opposite, because it wipes the disk.

questions.question: The bulk of a personal computer memory is the
questions.explanation: Most of a personal computer's main memory is RAM, which holds the operating system, programs and data in use. ROM (B) is only a small chip for start-up instructions, and registers (C) are a few tiny storage spots inside the CPU.

questions.question: One of the following is not a storage device
questions.explanation: A mouse is an input (pointing) device used to control the pointer on screen, so it does not store data. RAM (A) is memory, and floppy disks and Winchester (hard) disks (B and C) are storage media.

questions.question: ______ supervises the execution of instructions
questions.explanation: The control unit supervises and coordinates the execution of instructions, telling the other parts of the computer what to do and when. The ALU (A) carries out the calculations but does not supervise, and memory and ROM (B and E) only store data and instructions.

questions.question: ______ is not a peripheral unit
questions.explanation: Peripherals are devices attached outside the CPU and main memory, such as keyboards, disks, card readers and joysticks. Main memory is part of the central computer itself, so it is not a peripheral unit.

questions.question: ______ is not an example of impact printer
questions.explanation: Impact printers form characters by striking an inked ribbon against the paper, as line, daisy wheel, teletype and dot matrix printers do. An ink-jet printer sprays tiny drops of ink onto the paper without striking it, so it is a non-impact printer.

questions.question: What is the difference between hardware and software?

options.a: Hardware is tangible, but software is intangible.
options.b: Hardware is static, software is dynamic.
options.c: Hardware is metal, software is plastic.
options.d: Hardware is permanent, software is temporary.
options.e: Hardware is reliable, software is unreliable

questions.explanation: Hardware is made of physical, tangible parts you can touch, while software is a set of instructions with no physical form. Option C is wrong because hardware is not only metal and software is not plastic, and D and E are not true in general.

questions.question: Computer peripherals include ______ and ______ devices
questions.explanation: Peripherals are the input and output devices connected to a computer, such as keyboards, mice, printers and monitors. Control and logic (A) are functions of the CPU, not peripheral devices.

questions.question: MICR are suitable for reading magnetic inks on
questions.explanation: MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) reads characters printed in special magnetic ink, as used on bank cheques for the account and cheque numbers. Bank tellers (C) are people, not documents.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to read data on paper into the computer
questions.explanation: A scanner is an input device that reads text and pictures printed on paper and turns them into digital data. A mouse (A) only moves the pointer, a keyboard (E) takes typed input, and a compiler (B) is software, not a device.

questions.question: The mouse is used to perform the following operations
questions.explanation: A mouse is an input device used to point to and select objects on the screen, and in doing so it feeds input into the computer. It cannot scan objects into memory, which is the job of a scanner, so any option that includes B (such as D) is wrong. That leaves 'a and c only' as the full answer.

questions.question: The hardware components of a computer system does not include:
questions.explanation: COBOL is a programming language, which makes it software, not hardware. A printer, magnetic tape, light pen and RAM (A, B, C, E) are all physical parts or devices of a computer system.

questions.question: Which of the following is not part of the CPU?
questions.explanation: Tape is a secondary storage device that sits outside the CPU and is reached through input/output channels. The control unit and the ALU are the two main parts of the CPU, and registers are small, fast storage locations inside the CPU, so A, B and C are all part of it.

questions.question: CPU has elements of
questions.explanation: The CPU is made up of the control unit, which coordinates everything, and the arithmetic and logic unit, which does calculations and comparisons, so its elements are control, logic and arithmetic. Options A, B and D include secondary storage or communication, which are handled by devices outside the CPU.

questions.question: Formatting disk means

options.b: Preparing disk drive to accept floppy disk
options.c: Issuing commands to the operating system and the computer
options.d: Preparing disk for reading and writing in a computer

questions.explanation: Formatting prepares a disk so the computer can read from it and write to it, by laying out tracks and sectors and setting up a file system. It does not prepare the disk drive (B), and it is not just issuing commands (A, C).

questions.question: This is not true

options.a: Hard disk has large storage capacity
options.c: Hard disk is faster to access than floppy disk
options.d: Hard disk is usually fixed to the system unit
options.e: It is not wise to use hard disk, removable or not, as backup.

questions.explanation: Hard disks, both external and removable ones, are widely and sensibly used for backups, so the statement in E is the one that is not true. Statements A to D are correct: hard disks hold a lot, some are removable, they are faster than floppies and they are usually fixed inside the system unit. Option C is a true fact, which is why it cannot be the answer.

questions.question: A computer terminal refers to:
questions.explanation: A computer terminal is a device for putting data into a computer and getting results out, such as a keyboard with a screen. It is not the memory unit (A) or the CPU (B), which do the storing and processing.

questions.question: The computing power of a computer depends on

options.a: Clock speed designated by the mega hertz
options.b: Millions of instructions processed per second-MIPS

questions.explanation: Computing power is about how fast a computer can process instructions. Clock speed in megahertz and MIPS (millions of instructions per second) both measure this, so A and B are the answer. Hard disk size (C) tells you how much a computer can store, not how fast it works.

questions.question: One of the following is not capable of mass storage of data
questions.explanation: A 5.25-inch double-density diskette holds only a few hundred kilobytes, far too little to count as mass storage. Drums, disks, tapes and microfilm (A, C, D, E) were all used to store large amounts of data, and microfilm is a well-known way of archiving huge volumes of records.

questions.question: Identify the true statement here:

options.a: RAM and ROM have the same storage size
options.b: RAM is less than ROM in storage size
options.c: Storage is equal in size to RAM, ROM
options.d: ROM and RAM are parts of the Main memory

questions.explanation: Main (primary) memory is made up of RAM and ROM, so D is the true statement. RAM and ROM do not have the same size, and in practice RAM is usually much larger than ROM, so A and B are wrong.

questions.question: ______ is not an example of an input device
questions.explanation: Woofers are speakers, which are output devices that play sound. A keypunch machine, keyboard, light pen and flatbed scanner (A, C, D, E) are all used to enter data into a computer.

questions.question: The OCR method of input is best suited to one of the following applications
questions.explanation: OCR (optical character recognition) reads printed characters, so it suits turnaround documents like utility bills, where the printed bill comes back with the payment and is read by machine. Grading JAMB answer sheets (B) uses OMR, which detects shaded marks, while seat reservation and payroll (C, D) take input through terminals and files.

questions.question: What hardware components (of a typical desktop computer) are usually found inside of the systems unit?

options.a: The processor, main memory, and secondary memory
options.b: The processor, main memory, and monitor
options.d: The keyboard, the disks, and the audio blaster

questions.explanation: The system unit (the case) holds the processor, the main memory and secondary storage such as the hard disk. The monitor, keyboard and printer (B, D, E) are separate peripherals that connect from outside.

questions.question: Where are programs and data kept while the processor is using them?
questions.explanation: While the processor is working on programs and data, they are held in main memory (RAM), which the CPU can reach directly and quickly. Secondary memory such as disk or tape (B, C, D) keeps them for the long term, but they must be loaded into main memory before the CPU can use them.

questions.question: How is it possible that both programs and data can be stored on the same floppy disk?

options.a: Floppy disks can only store programs, not data
options.b: Programs and data are both software, and both can be stored on any memory device
options.c: A floppy disk has to be formatted for one or for the other
options.d: Floppy disks can only store data, not programs
options.e: A floppy disk has two sides, one for data and one for programs

questions.explanation: Programs and data are both just patterns of bits, so any storage device, including a floppy disk, can hold either. A floppy does not have to be formatted for one or the other (C), and its two sides are not split between programs and data (E).

questions.question: Why does a computer have a clock?

options.a: The state of binary signals is measured only at specific instants in time
options.b: A clock is needed to check how fast signals are changing
options.c: A clock is needed to check that voltage levels are correct
options.d: A clock is used only with application programs that need to know the current time
options.e: A clock is used to generate random numbers for the computer

questions.explanation: A computer's clock sends out regular pulses, and the states of the binary signals are read only at those exact moments, which keeps all the parts of the computer in step. It is not there to measure how fast signals change (B) or to check voltages (C), and it is not only for programs that need the time of day (D).

questions.question: What part of a computer system is most directly concerned with performing the actions called for by a program?
questions.explanation: The processor (CPU) is the part that actually carries out a program's instructions, which is why it is called the brain of the computer. Main memory (B) only holds the program and data, while the hard disk, monitor and mouse (A, D, E) are storage and input/output devices.

questions.question: What is a machine operation

options.a: Any activity of any part of the computer system
options.b: One of the tiny electronic operations that a processor can perform
options.c: A section of main memory that is part of a computer program
options.d: An activity of the operating system needed to run a program.
options.e: A flip of the machine time

questions.explanation: A machine operation is one of the small basic electronic actions a processor can carry out directly, such as adding two numbers or moving data. It is not any activity in the system (A), and it is not an operating-system task (D).

questions.question: A computer terminal refers to

options.e: Input, Output, and Central Processing Unit

questions.explanation: A terminal is the equipment a user works at to put data in and get results out, usually a keyboard with a screen. It handles both input and output, so A and B are each only half right, and it does not include the CPU (C, E).

questions.question: A classic example of data capture is the usage of
questions.explanation: An OMR (optical mark reader) scanner is a classic data capture device: it reads shaded marks on forms such as exam answer sheets directly into the computer, with no typing needed. A laser printer and a plotter (C, D) are output devices, and an offline sorter (A) only arranges documents, so All of the above (E) cannot be right.

questions.question: ____ is any part of the computer that you can physically touch
questions.explanation: Hardware means the physical parts of a computer that you can see and touch, such as the keyboard, monitor and CPU. A peripheral (A) and a device (D) are only some kinds of hardware, and an application (E) is software.

questions.question: Below are the basic components of a computer:

options.a: Input devices, processing unit, storage, and output devices
options.d: Input devices, output devices, printing, and typing

questions.explanation: A computer is built from four basic parts: input devices to bring data in, a processing unit to work on it, storage to keep it, and output devices to show results. Option B leaves out output, C lists only input and output devices with no processing or storage, and D lists activities (printing, typing) rather than components.

questions.question: The result of arithmetic and logical operations are stored in?
questions.explanation: The accumulator is a register inside the CPU that holds the results of arithmetic and logic operations as they are worked out. The control unit (A) directs operations rather than storing results, and ROM (B) holds permanent instructions.

questions.question: Secondary storage device is needed to?

options.e: Store large volume of data that exceed the capacity of main memory

questions.explanation: Secondary storage is used to keep large volumes of data permanently, more than the main memory can hold. Arithmetic and logic (C) are done by the ALU, control (D) is done by the control unit, and printing (B) is an output job.

questions.question: Which of the following is not considered a hardware?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Word is a program, so it is software, not hardware. The hard disk, keyboard, CPU and mouse are all physical parts you can touch.

questions.question: Which among the following has low speed storage?
questions.explanation: Magnetic tape stores data one item after another along its length, so finding a particular record means winding through the tape, which makes it slow. Magnetic disks, flash drives and CD-ROMs (A, B, D) can jump directly to the data they need.

questions.question: Consider the following: I Operating System; II Control Unit; III Main memory; IV Arithmetic and Logic Unit. The Central Processing Unit (CPU) consists of
questions.explanation: The CPU is made up of the Control Unit, which directs operations, and the Arithmetic and Logic Unit, which does calculations and comparisons, so II and IV are correct. The operating system (I) is software, not part of the CPU, which rules out C and D.

questions.question: How many 3.5-inch floppy disks can you get in 432MB?
questions.explanation: A standard high-density 3.5-inch floppy disk holds 1.44 MB, so 432 MB divided by 1.44 MB = 300 disks. Options A and B (350, 320) would only be right if each disk held less than 1.44 MB.

questions.question: The personal computer and the Apple Macintosh are examples of two different ____
questions.explanation: A platform is the combination of hardware and operating system that software runs on, and the PC (Windows) and the Apple Macintosh are two different platforms. Options A, B and E describe software that runs on a platform, not the platform itself. Option C, storage program, is not a standard term.

questions.question: ____ is an operating system that supports single user process and single thread.
questions.explanation: MS-DOS is a single-user, single-tasking operating system, so it runs one program for one user at a time. Option C, UNIX, is a multi-user, multitasking system, and option B, Windows, supports multitasking. Option A, OS/2, also supports multitasking and multithreading.

questions.question: ____ is the only language a computer can process directly without a previous transformation.
questions.explanation: Machine code is made up of binary instructions (0s and 1s) that the CPU can understand and execute directly. Option E, assembly language, still needs an assembler to turn it into machine code. Options A, B and D are high-level languages that must be compiled or interpreted first.

questions.question: The two broad categories of software are ____ and ____.
questions.explanation: Software is broadly divided into system software, which runs the computer, and application software, which helps users do specific tasks. Option D names two kinds of application software, and option B names two operating systems, which are both system software. Option A is wrong because transaction is not a broad category of software.

questions.question: Computers process data under the control of sets of instructions termed?
questions.explanation: A computer program is a set of instructions that tells the computer what to do and how to process data. Option C, computer instructions, are the individual steps inside a program, but the whole controlling set is called a program. Options A, B and D are buses, bits and data, which are not instructions.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an example of operating system?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Office XP is an office suite, which is application software for tasks like word processing and spreadsheets. Options A, B, D and E (BSD UNIX, Red Hat Linux, Android and Windows 98) are all operating systems.

questions.question: What type of software is used to manage computer hardware and software resources?
questions.explanation: System software, especially the operating system, manages the computer's hardware and provides a platform for other software to run. Option C, utility software, is a part of system software that does maintenance jobs, so it is not the full answer. Option A, application software, is for user tasks, not resource management.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a computer language?
questions.explanation: Linux is an operating system, a piece of system software that runs the computer, so it is not a computer language at all. Python and Java (options A and B) are programming languages, HTML (option C) is a markup language for building web pages, and SQL (option D) is a query language for databases. All four of those are languages you write instructions in, which is why E is the odd one out.

questions.question: Which programming language was developed in the 1970s and is the basis for many modern programming languages?
questions.explanation: The C language was developed in the early 1970s and strongly influenced later languages such as C++, Java and C#. Options A and B, FORTRAN and COBOL, came out in the 1950s, option D, BASIC, came out in the 1960s, and option E, Java, came out in the 1990s.

questions.question: A program that translates high-level language into machine language line by line is called
questions.explanation: An interpreter translates a high-level program into machine language one line at a time, running each line as it goes. Option A, a compiler, translates the whole program at once, and option C, an assembler, translates assembly language, not high-level language.

questions.question: The term "bug" in computing refers to

options.b: A unit for measuring processing speed

questions.explanation: A bug is an error or flaw in a program that makes it behave wrongly, and finding and fixing bugs is called debugging. Option A, malware, is software written on purpose to cause harm, which is different from an accidental mistake in code. Option D is tempting, but a hardware fault is usually called a fault or failure, not a bug.

questions.question: A computer language that is closer to human languages is called
questions.explanation: High-level languages like Python, Java and Visual Basic use English-like words, so they are closer to human language. Options A, B, D and E are low-level forms that are much closer to the machine's binary instructions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of software?
questions.explanation: Hardware means the physical parts of a computer, so it is not a type of software. Operating systems, application software, system software and utility software (options A, B, C and E) are all types of software.

questions.question: What is the main function of the operating system?

options.b: To control the computer's hardware and software resources

questions.explanation: The operating system controls the computer's hardware and software resources and acts as a link between the user and the machine. Option A, performing arithmetic, is done by the ALU, and option C, compiling languages, is done by compilers. Displaying graphics and connecting to the internet (options D and E) are handled by other hardware and software.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a utility software?
questions.explanation: Antivirus software is a utility program because it helps maintain and protect the computer system from malware. Web browsers, spreadsheets, word processors and graphics editors (options A, B, D and E) are application software for user tasks.

questions.question: A software that helps you manage files, perform system maintenance tasks, and manage disk drives is called
questions.explanation: Utility software helps maintain the computer, for example by managing files, cleaning or defragmenting disks and backing up data. Option C, system software, is the broad group utilities belong to, so it is less specific. Option D, antivirus software, is only one kind of utility.

questions.question: What are the stages in the compilation process?

options.a: Feasibility study, system design and testing
options.c: Lexical Analysis, syntax analysis, and code generation

questions.explanation: A compiler works in stages: lexical analysis breaks the code into tokens, syntax analysis checks the grammar, and code generation produces machine code. Options A and B list stages of system development, not compilation.

questions.question: Software in computer

options.a: Enhances the capabilities of the hardware machine
options.b: Increase the speed of central processing unit

questions.explanation: Software makes the hardware useful by telling it what tasks to perform, so it enhances the machine's capabilities. Option B is wrong because software does not change the CPU's physical speed, so option C is also wrong.

questions.question: Mnemonic a memory trick is used in which of the following language?
questions.explanation: Assembly language uses mnemonics, short memory aids like ADD or MOV, to stand for machine instructions. Option A, machine language, uses only binary codes, and option C, high-level languages, use English-like statements.

questions.question: Instruction in computer languages consists of
questions.explanation: A machine instruction has two parts: the opcode, which says what operation to perform, and the operand, which gives the data or address to work on. Since it needs both, option C is correct.

questions.question: The word processing task associated with changing the appearance of a document is
questions.explanation: Formatting changes how a document looks, such as its font, size, colour, margins and alignment. Option A, editing, changes the content itself by adding, deleting or correcting text. Option B, writing, means entering the text.

questions.question: A compiler is a translating program which

options.a: Translates instruction of a high level language into machine language
options.b: Translates entire source program into machine language program
options.c: It is not involved in program's execution

questions.explanation: A compiler translates high-level language into machine language, it translates the whole program at once, and it is not needed while the finished program runs. Since A, B and C are all true, option D is correct.

questions.question: Programs designed to perform specific tasks is known as
questions.explanation: Application software is designed to perform specific user tasks, such as word processing or keeping accounts. Options A and D, system software and the operating system, run the computer itself. Option C, utilities, maintain the system.

questions.question: Which of the following is not anti-viruses software?
questions.explanation: Oracle is mainly known for database software, not antivirus software. NAV (Norton AntiVirus), F-Prot and McAfee (options A, B and D) are all antivirus programs.

questions.question: What is a compiler?

options.a: A compiler does a conversion line by line as the program is run
options.b: A compiler converts the whole of a higher level program code into machine code in one step
options.c: A compiler is a general purpose language providing very efficient execution

questions.explanation: A compiler converts the whole high-level program into machine code in one go before it is run. Option A describes an interpreter, which translates line by line while the program runs. Option C describes a language, not a translator.

questions.question: Which of the following is machine independence program?
questions.explanation: High-level languages are machine independent: the same program can run on different computers after it is translated. Options B, C and D (low-level, assembly and machine languages) are tied to a particular processor.

questions.question: FORTRAN programming language is more suitable for
questions.explanation: FORTRAN (FORmula TRANslation) was designed for scientific and engineering calculations. Option A, business applications, is the area COBOL was designed for.

questions.question: An error in software or hardware is called a bug. What is the alternative computer jargon for it?
questions.explanation: Glitch is another common computer term for a bug, meaning a fault that makes software or hardware misbehave. Options A, B and C (leech, squid and slug) are not terms for errors.

questions.question: Operating system, editors, and debuggers comes under?
questions.explanation: System software supports the running and development of programs, and this includes the operating system as well as programming tools like editors and debuggers. Option B, application software, is for end-user tasks such as word processing, and option C, utilities, is only one part of system software.

questions.question: Which programming languages are classified as low level languages?
questions.explanation: Assembly language is a low level language because it uses short mnemonics that map almost one-to-one onto machine instructions. Option A lists BASIC, COBOL and FORTRAN, which are high level languages, and options B and C refer to artificial intelligence tools, not low level languages.

questions.question: What is an interpreter?

options.a: An interpreter does the conversion line by line as the program is run
options.b: An interpreter is the representation of the system being designed
options.c: An interpreter is a general purpose language providing very efficient execution

questions.explanation: An interpreter translates and runs a high level program one line at a time while the program is being executed. Option B describes a model or design document, not a translator, and option C is wrong because interpreters are usually slower than compiled programs.

questions.question: A directly accessible appointment calendar is a feature of a ____ resident package
questions.explanation: A memory resident program stays loaded in main memory so it can be called up instantly, which is how a pop-up appointment calendar could be used at any time. Options A and D (CPU and ALU) process instructions rather than hold programs, and option C, a buffer, only holds data temporarily during transfers.

questions.question: What is the first stage in software development?
questions.explanation: Software development normally begins with system analysis, where the existing system and user requirements are studied before anything is designed. Option A, specification and design, follows analysis, and testing and maintenance (B and D) come near the end of the cycle.

questions.question: The translator program used in assembly language is called
questions.explanation: An assembler translates assembly language programs into machine code. A compiler and an interpreter (A and B) translate high level languages, and option D, translator, is only the general name for all three types.

questions.question: which of the following is problem oriented language?
questions.explanation: High level languages are problem-oriented because they let programmers describe the problem in English-like terms without worrying about machine details. Machine language, assembly language and low level languages (B, C and D) are all machine-oriented.

questions.question: An error in computer data is called
questions.explanation: A bug is an error or fault in a computer program or data that causes wrong results. Options A, C and D are hardware parts, not errors.

questions.question: A Compiler is

options.b: a program which translates from one high-level language to another
options.c: a program which translates from one high-level to a machine level language

questions.explanation: A compiler translates a whole high level program into machine language in one go before it is run. Option B describes translating between two high level languages, which is not what a compiler normally does, and option A is not a program at all.

questions.question: Which of the following is not computer language?
questions.explanation: Computer languages are classed as high level or low level, so medium level is not a standard category. Options A and C are real categories, which also rules out option D. Some people informally call C a middle-level language, but that is not a recognised class.

questions.question: The programs which are as permanent as hardware and stored in ROM is known as
questions.explanation: Firmware is software permanently stored in ROM, so it is almost as fixed as hardware. Option A, hardware, means physical parts, and option B, software, normally refers to programs that can be easily changed or replaced.

questions.question: What do you call the translator which takes assembly language program as input & produce machine language code as output?
questions.explanation: An assembler converts assembly language programs into machine code. A compiler and an interpreter (A and B) translate high level languages, and a debugger (C) helps find errors rather than translating code.

questions.question: An application program that helps the user to change any number and immediately see the result of that change is
questions.explanation: A spreadsheet recalculates formulas automatically, so when you change one number you immediately see the effect on every related result. Desktop publishing and databases (A and B) are for page layout and storing records, not instant what-if calculations.

questions.question: A computer program that converts an entire program into machine language at one time is called a/an
questions.explanation: A compiler translates an entire high level program into machine language at one time, before it runs. Option A, an interpreter, translates and runs the program one line at a time.

questions.question: FORTRAN is a programming language. What does FORTRAN stand for?
questions.explanation: FORTRAN stands for FORmula TRANslation, a high level language created for scientific and engineering calculations. File, Format and Floppy Translation (A, B and D) are not real expansions.

questions.question: A collection of related instructions organized for a common purpose is referred to as
questions.explanation: A program is a set of related instructions arranged to carry out a particular task. A file (option A) is any named collection of stored data, and a database (option B) is an organised collection of records.

questions.question: Which language is directly understood by the computer without translation program?
questions.explanation: Machine language is written in binary 0s and 1s that the CPU can execute directly, without any translation. Assembly language (option B) needs an assembler, and high level languages (option C) need a compiler or interpreter.

questions.question: High level language is also called
questions.explanation: High-level languages are called problem-oriented languages because they let the programmer describe the problem in English-like terms instead of machine details. Business-oriented (B) describes COBOL and mathematically oriented (C) describes FORTRAN, which are only particular high-level languages, so D is not right.

questions.question: Which statement is valid about interpreter?

options.a: It translates one instruction at a time
options.b: Object code is saved for future use

questions.explanation: An interpreter translates and executes one instruction (line) at a time. Saving object code for future use (B) and not needing repeated translation (C) describe a compiler, so D is also wrong.

questions.question: Which is the limitation of high level language?
questions.explanation: High-level languages are less efficient because the translated machine code is usually slower and uses more memory than hand-written low-level code. Machine dependence and machine-level coding (B, C) are drawbacks of low-level languages, not high-level ones.

questions.question: In which language is source program written?
questions.explanation: A source program is the program as the programmer writes it, usually in a high-level language, before it is translated into machine code. Machine code (B) is the output of that translation (the object program), not the source, and plain English (A) and 'temporary' (D) are not programming languages.

questions.question: A computer Program that translates one program instruction at a time into machine language is called a/an
questions.explanation: An interpreter translates and executes a program one instruction (line) at a time. A compiler (C) translates the whole program at once, while the CPU and a simulator (B, D) do not do translation.

questions.question: Which of the following is a programming language?
questions.explanation: Pascal is a programming language used for writing programs. Lotus and MS-Excel (A, C) are spreadsheet applications, and Netscape (D) is a web browser.

questions.question: The language that the computer can understand and execute is called
questions.explanation: Machine language, made of binary 0s and 1s, is the only language the computer can understand and execute directly. Application software and system programs (B, C) are written in other languages and must be translated into machine language.

questions.question: Which of the following is called low level languages?
questions.explanation: Machine language (binary instructions) and assembly language (short mnemonics that map directly to machine instructions) are both low-level languages because they are close to the hardware. That makes C correct; choosing only A or only B leaves out the other low-level language.

questions.question: Each model of a computer has a unique
questions.explanation: Machine language is the set of binary instructions a particular processor understands directly, so it differs from one computer model or processor family to another. High-level languages (C) are designed to be machine-independent, which is why the same program can run on different computers.

questions.question: Any method for controlling access to or use of memory is known as
questions.explanation: Memory protection is any method that controls which programs can access or use particular areas of memory, so one program cannot damage another's data. Memory management (C) is the wider job of allocating memory, and a memory map (A) is just a layout of memory addresses.

questions.question: Who invented the high level language C?
questions.explanation: Dennis M. Ritchie created the C language at Bell Labs in the early 1970s. Niklaus Wirth (B) designed Pascal, Seymour Papert (C) co-created Logo, and Donald Knuth (D) is famous for his books on algorithms and the TeX system.

questions.question: What do you call the programs that are used to find out possible faults and their causes?
questions.explanation: Diagnostic software tests a computer's hardware and software to find faults and their causes. Cookies (B) are small files websites store in a browser, and boot diskettes (D) are used to start a computer, not to find faults.

questions.question: A compiler is
questions.explanation: A compiler is a language translator that converts a whole high-level program into machine code in one go. An assembler (A) translates assembly language, and an interpreter (E) translates line by line, so they are other kinds of translators rather than what a compiler is. Object code (B) is the output a compiler produces.

questions.question: What type of software is an anti-virus software
questions.explanation: Antivirus software is utility software, a program that helps maintain and protect the computer, like disk cleanup and backup tools. It is not application software (C), which does user tasks such as word processing, and it is not an operating system (D). Microsoft Office (A) is an application package, not a type of software.

questions.question: The operating system is the most common type of ________ software
questions.explanation: The operating system is the main example of system software, because it manages the hardware and provides a platform for other programs. Application software (D) such as word processors runs on top of the operating system, and memory (C) is hardware, not a type of software.

questions.question: Which of the following is designed to control the operations of a computer?
questions.explanation: System software, especially the operating system, controls and coordinates the hardware and the operations of the computer. Application software (B) does user tasks, and utility software (A) is only a part of system software that handles maintenance jobs.

questions.question: Which of the following executes its programming codes line by line, rather than executing the whole program as a whole?
questions.explanation: An interpreter translates and runs a program one line at a time. A compiler (E) translates the whole program in one go before it is run, and a linker (B) joins compiled pieces of code into one executable file.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a computer language?
questions.explanation: Lotus (Lotus 1-2-3) was a spreadsheet application, not a programming language. FORTRAN, COBOL, BASIC and C++ (B to E) are all programming languages.

questions.question: Which is the LINUX operating system?
questions.explanation: Linux is an open-source operating system: its source code is free for anyone to view, change and share. Closed-source and proprietary systems (B and E) keep their code private, and Linux is not Windows (C).

questions.question: What is the role of an operating system in a computer?

options.b: To oversee hardware and software interactions

questions.explanation: The operating system manages the hardware and acts as the link between the hardware, the application software and the user. It does not build hardware (A) or write user applications (C), and long-term storage (D) is the job of storage devices.

questions.question: Software can be classified into:
questions.explanation: Software is divided into system software, which runs the computer, and application software, which carries out tasks for the user. Input and output devices (A) are hardware, and C and D are not the standard classes of software.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of system software?
questions.explanation: Windows is an operating system, the main kind of system software, and it manages the computer's resources. Word processors (A), photo editors (C) and browsers (D) are application software that do particular jobs for the user.

questions.question: A programming language is:

options.b: A tool for crafting software programs

questions.explanation: A programming language is a set of words and grammar rules for writing instructions, so it is a tool for creating software. It is not a physical component (C) or a storage medium (D), and it is not limited to hardware instructions (A).

questions.question: Which of the following is a high-level programming language?
questions.explanation: Python is a high-level language because its code reads much like English and does not depend on a particular machine. Machine code (A), assembly code (B) and binary instructions (D) are low-level and close to the hardware.

questions.question: The main difference between high-level and low-level languages is:

options.b: Low-level languages are simpler to master

questions.explanation: High-level languages are written in words and symbols close to human language, while low-level languages are close to the machine's own instructions. It is true that high-level programs can run a bit more slowly (C), but that is a side effect, not the main difference. Low-level languages are harder to learn (B) and less portable (D), not more.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of application software?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Excel is application software that lets users work with spreadsheets. Unix (A) is an operating system, while BIOS (C) and device drivers (D) are system-level software that support the hardware.

questions.question: The process of converting high-level code into machine code is called:
questions.explanation: Compilation is the process of translating a whole high-level program into machine code that the computer can run. Interpreting (D) also translates code, but it does so line by line as the program runs instead of producing a machine-code version. Running (B) and correcting errors (C) are not translation.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of machine language?
questions.explanation: Machine language is made up of binary sequences of 0s and 1s that the CPU can carry out directly. It is hard for people to read (A), it differs from one processor to another (C), and it is the least abstract kind of language (D).

questions.question: An interpreter differs from a compiler because it:

options.a: Processes the full program at once
options.d: Saves the program for later use

questions.explanation: An interpreter translates and runs a program line by line as it goes. A compiler is the one that processes the whole program at once (A) and saves the translated version to run later (D).

questions.question: Which of the following programming languages was developed first?
questions.explanation: FORTRAN was released in 1957, making it the oldest of these languages. C++ came in the mid-1980s, Python in 1991 and Java in 1995, so options A, B and D all came decades later.

questions.question: Firmware is:
questions.explanation: Firmware is software stored permanently in a hardware chip, such as the BIOS in ROM, to control the device. It is not an app the user installs (A), a coding standard (C) or a kind of operating system (D).

questions.question: Which of these operating systems is owned by Google?
questions.explanation: Android is the mobile operating system developed and owned by Google, used on most smartphones. Windows (option A) belongs to Microsoft and Mac OS (option B) belongs to Apple. Unix (option D) came from Bell Labs, and Linux (option E) is a free system started by Linus Torvalds.

questions.question: Short programs or instructions written by the manufacturer in order to start up the computer system are called ____.
