questions.question: which of the following is the save icon
questions.explanation: The Save icon is drawn as a diskette (floppy disk), because files used to be saved to floppies. The folder icon (B) usually means Open, and the scissors icon (A) means Cut.

questions.question: which of the following is an integer data type
questions.explanation: An integer is a whole number with no fractional part, so 30 is an integer value. 6.5 and 24.22 (A, C) have decimal parts, X-1 (D) is an expression and "Sam" (E) is a string.

questions.question: What are Control Arrays?

options.a: Arrays that are in a particular order
options.b: Multiple controls of the same type that can be grouped into arrays
options.e: These are arrays controlled by their data types

questions.explanation: A control array is a group of controls of the same type, for example several text boxes, that share one name and are told apart by an Index number. It has nothing to do with the order of data (A) or with control statements (C).

questions.question: A ______ is created by placing a control within the form design window and assigning a value 0 to its index property
questions.explanation: Setting a control's Index property to 0 makes it the first element of a control array, and more controls of the same type can then be added with the same name. Dynamic arrays (A) are variables resized with ReDim, not controls.

questions.question: which of the following can not be found in a tool box
questions.explanation: The toolbox holds controls such as command buttons, picture boxes, frames and option buttons (A to D). Properties are set in the separate Properties window, so a 'property box' is not in the toolbox.

questions.question: What are the three basic controls in visual basic?
questions.explanation: The text box, command button and label are the three basic Visual Basic controls: the text box takes input, the command button triggers actions and the label shows text. The other options swap in less basic controls like the check box, combo box or picture box.

questions.question: Visual basic toolbox include the following except?
questions.explanation: Text box, label, command button and frame (A, B, C, E) are all controls in the Visual Basic toolbox. Print is a statement or method used in code, not a toolbox control.

questions.question: The most straightforward way to display output data is with?
questions.explanation: Labels and text boxes are the simplest way to show output in Visual Basic, because you just assign the result to their Caption or Text property. Option and command buttons (A) are for choices and actions, not for showing data.

questions.question: The method of adding control to the form design windows are
questions.explanation: There are two ways to put a control on a form: double-click its tool in the toolbox so it appears at a default size, or click the tool and then drag on the form to draw it. Option E only describes the second method, so B is the complete answer. Right-clicking (A, C, D) is not how controls are added.

questions.question: Which of the following holds text that appear on the command button
questions.explanation: The Caption property holds the text shown on a command button, such as 'OK' or 'Calculate'. ToolTipText (E) is the small hint that pops up when the mouse hovers over the button.

questions.question: Which of the following properties determines whether command button is active
questions.explanation: The Enabled property decides whether a command button is active: when it is True the button can be clicked, and when it is False the button is greyed out and does nothing. Visible (B) only decides whether the button can be seen at all, while Default and Cancel (D, E) link the button to the Enter and Esc keys.

questions.question: Which of the following properties enlarges the labels size properties
questions.explanation: When a label's AutoSize property is True, the label automatically resizes to fit its caption. Width (E) can be set by hand, but it does not adjust automatically, and Alignment (A) only positions the text.

questions.question: The shape of the mouse cursor is determined by
questions.explanation: The MousePointer property sets the shape of the mouse cursor over an object, for example an arrow, an hourglass or a crosshair. The other options are not real Visual Basic properties.

questions.question: ---------- specifies the order of the text box in focus order
questions.explanation: TabIndex sets a text box's position in the focus order, deciding when it gets focus as the user presses Tab. TabStop (A) only decides whether the control can get focus by tabbing at all.

questions.question: F1 on the key board is used for
questions.explanation: F1 is the standard key for opening Help in Windows programs, including Visual Basic. F5 runs a program in Visual Basic, so C is wrong.

questions.question: In visual basic data falls into three broad categories
questions.explanation: Visual Basic data is commonly grouped into numeric data (numbers), string data (text) and special data (such as dates, Boolean values and Variant). The other options mix terms that overlap, like string and alphanumeric, or are not data categories at all.

questions.question: When visual basic converts one data type to another it is called
questions.explanation: Changing a value from one data type to another, for example turning the number 5 into the text "5", is called conversion. Implicit typing (C) is about a variable getting a type without being declared, which is a different idea, and 'changing' (B) is not the technical term, so D and E do not fit either.

questions.question: ---------- is a series of zero or more characters that you treat as a single entity.
questions.explanation: A string is a series of zero or more characters, such as "Abass" or even an empty "", that is treated as a single item of data. Numeric data (A) holds numbers that can be used in arithmetic.

questions.question: ---------- returns a string data value that holds the data typed by the user.
questions.explanation: The InputBox function shows a prompt, waits for the user to type something and returns what they typed as a string, which you can store in a variable. MsgBox (A) shows a message and returns only which button was clicked, not typed data.

questions.question: Visual Basic translates source program into
questions.explanation: Visual Basic compiles the code you write into an executable program (an .exe file) that the computer can run. A flowchart (A) is a planning diagram drawn before coding, and plain text, pictures or shapes (B, D, E) are not what a translator produces.

questions.question: ---------- supplies controls
questions.explanation: The Toolbox supplies the controls, such as text boxes, labels and command buttons, that you place on a form. A dialog box (A) is used to talk to the user, and 'DataBox' (C) is not a Visual Basic window.

questions.question: What property disables a textbox from triggering events when the user types or clicks the textbox
questions.explanation: Setting a text box's Enabled property to False stops it from responding to typing or clicks, so none of its events fire. TabIndex and TabStop (A and C) only control the order and whether the box is reached with the Tab key, and Alignment (D) just positions the text.

questions.question: What are two controls that behave as if they conform to Boolean datatype
questions.explanation: Option buttons and check boxes behave like Boolean values because each one is simply on or off (selected or not selected). A command button (option A) just triggers an action when clicked, and a text box (C) holds text, so neither works like a True/False value.

questions.question: Which of the following variable names is written incorrectly?
questions.explanation: A variable name may contain only letters, digits and the underscore, and must start with a letter, so x.7 is wrong because of the full stop. root1, xmax, c3 and CustomerName all follow the rules.

questions.question: Which of the following string items is written correctly?
questions.explanation: A string constant must be enclosed in a pair of double quotes, which is exactly how "July 4, 1776" is written. Option B has extra quotes inside the string, C is missing its closing quote, D has no quotes at all, and E uses single quotes, which VB treats as the start of a comment.

questions.question: What is the result of the function Len(Address) on the given expression Address= "Faculty Of Science"?
questions.explanation: Len counts every character in the string, spaces included. "Faculty Of Science" has 7 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 7 = 18 characters. Option A (16) forgets to count the two spaces.

questions.question: What is the result of the function Lcase(Address) on Address= "Faculty Of Science"?
questions.explanation: LCase converts every letter in a string to lower case, so "Faculty Of Science" becomes "faculty of science". Option A is what UCase would return, and C and E only change some of the letters.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid VB integer?
questions.explanation: A VB Integer is a whole number with no decimal part, stored in 2 bytes, so it must lie between -32768 and 32767; 32766 is a whole number inside that range. Options A to D all have a decimal part, so they are not integers, and C and D also contain commas, which VB does not accept inside a number.

questions.question: Which of the following assignment statements is wrong?
questions.explanation: In VB an assignment uses a plain equals sign, as in y = a + b; the := symbol belongs to languages like Pascal, so option C is wrong. The others correctly assign a value, a caption string or a joined string to a variable or property.

questions.question: What is the result of the following operation Int(-2.3)?
questions.explanation: Int returns the largest whole number that is less than or equal to its argument, so for negative numbers it moves down, not toward zero. The largest whole number not greater than -2.3 is -3. Option B leaves the number unchanged, and -2 is not offered because Int does not simply chop off the decimal.

questions.question: What is the result of the following operation Int(-3.7)
questions.explanation: Int always rounds down to the next whole number that is not larger than the argument. For -3.7 that is -4, because -3 would be larger than -3.7. Option A leaves the number unchanged, and B and C drop the minus sign.

questions.question: The following operations can be carried out on strings except:
questions.explanation: Abs gives the absolute (positive) value of a number, so it works on numeric data, not on strings. LCase, Left, Len and Mid (A, B, C and E) are all string functions that change, measure or extract parts of text.

questions.question: The maximum permissible length of a variable name is:
questions.explanation: One of the rules for naming a variable in Visual Basic is that the name can be no more than 255 characters long. Option C (256) is a close distractor but is one character too many, and the other figures do not match the rule.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a data type in VB?
questions.explanation: Integer, Double, Currency and Date are all real VB data types. There is no Triple type; the name is a made-up distractor based on Single and Double.

questions.question: The following are reserved words in VB except:
questions.explanation: Dim, If, Else and Case are all reserved words that VB uses in declarations and decision statements. When is not a VB keyword, so it could actually be used as an ordinary name.

questions.question: The following operations can be performed on numeric variables except:
questions.explanation: UCase converts letters in a string to upper case, so it only makes sense for text, not numbers. Abs, Log, Cos and Exp (A, B, D and E) are mathematical functions used on numeric values.

questions.question: Which of the following keywords is used to declare variables?
questions.explanation: Dim is the keyword used to declare a variable, as in Dim Surname As String. Declare, Define, Definite and Demo are not used for declaring ordinary variables in VB.

questions.question: Which windows displays a list of all forms and modules making up your application?
questions.explanation: The Project window lists all the forms and modules that make up your VB application. The Properties window (A) sets values for the selected object, and the Form Layout window (C) shows where the form will appear on the screen.

questions.question: The rectangle shape in the flow chart diagram is used for what?
questions.explanation: In a flowchart, a rectangle represents a processing step, such as a calculation or assignment. Start and stop (A, C) use an oval terminal symbol, a decision (E) uses a diamond, and arrows show the logic flow (D).

questions.question: When you open the visual studio environment, what do you select to develop a calculator?
questions.explanation: To build a calculator with buttons and text boxes in Visual Studio, you create a new Windows Forms Application project, which gives you a form to draw controls on. The other options are not project types you select to start a new application.

questions.question: Which property determines whether a control is displayed to the user in Visual Basic?
questions.explanation: The Visible property decides whether a control is shown: True displays it and False hides it. Enabled (E) only decides whether the control responds to the user while it stays on screen; Show, Hide and Disabled are not this property.

questions.question: An algorithm represented in the form of a programming language is known as
questions.explanation: Once an algorithm is written out in a programming language, it becomes a program that the computer can run. Pseudocode (D) and a flowchart (C) are ways of describing an algorithm before it is written in an actual programming language.

questions.question: If you dont want the content of the text box changed what do you do?

options.a: click on the text box, go to Enabled and choose False
options.b: click on the label box, go to Enabled and choose False
options.d: click on the form, go to Enabled and choose True
options.e: click on the text box, go to Enabled and choose True

questions.explanation: Setting a text box's Enabled property to False stops the user from typing in it or changing its content. Option B changes a label, not the text box, and D and E set Enabled to True, which leaves everything editable. Doing nothing (C) keeps the text box open to changes.

questions.question: _____ is a type of diagram that represents an algorithm or process, showing the steps as boxes of various kinds, and their order by connecting these with arrows?
questions.explanation: A flowchart is a diagram that shows the steps of an algorithm as boxes of different shapes, connected by arrows to show their order. An algorithm (A) is the list of steps itself, and bar charts and histograms (B, D) display data, not processes.

questions.question: The CancelButton is a property that belongs to ____ object.
questions.explanation: CancelButton is a property of a Form: it names the button that is clicked when the user presses the Esc key. Buttons, labels and text boxes do not have this property themselves.

questions.question: The pseudocode is another name for
questions.explanation: Pseudocode is a way of writing an algorithm in plain, English-like steps, which is why it is treated as another name for the algorithm itself. Object code and executable code (A, C) are translated machine versions of a program, and a flowchart (E) shows the algorithm as a diagram instead.

questions.question: What is text box used for in the Visual Basic environment

options.e: Are used to accept input from the user

questions.explanation: A text box is the control used to accept input typed by the user (and it can also show text). A label is the control normally used just to display text, which is why option D is not the best answer.

questions.question: The small circle shape in the flow chart diagram is used for what?
questions.explanation: In a flowchart, a small circle is a connector, used to join parts of the chart that are far apart or on different pages. Start and stop (B) use an oval, processing (D) uses a rectangle and a decision (E) uses a diamond.

questions.question: Which of these is not among the stages involved in programming?

options.b: Analysis of the problem and modelling

questions.explanation: Defining the problem, analysing and modelling it, choosing or designing an algorithm, and documenting the program are all standard stages of programming. Since every listed option is a real stage, the answer is None of the options.

questions.question: The terminal symbol in a flowchart indicates
questions.explanation: The terminal symbol is the oval shape that marks where a flowchart starts or ends, and End is the only one of those offered here. Input and output (A) use a parallelogram, a decision (C) uses a diamond, and processing (E) uses a rectangle, while flow (D) is shown with arrows.

questions.question: What is an Event

options.c: it is an action recognised by an object for which code can be written
options.d: it is an action recognised by an object for which code cannot be written

questions.explanation: An event is an action, such as a click or key press, that an object recognizes and for which you can write code to respond. Option D is wrong because the whole point of an event is that code can be written for it.

questions.question: Numbers without the decimal points are
questions.explanation: Integers are numbers with no decimal point, such as 5, -12 or 0. Real numbers (A) can have decimal parts, and strings and characters (B, E) are text rather than numbers.

questions.question: What are labels used for in the Visual Basic environment?

options.c: Are used to accept input from the user

questions.explanation: A label is used to display text, such as a title or a result, that the user cannot edit directly. Accepting input from the user (C) is the job of a text box.

questions.question: In event-driven programming, an event is generated by ____
questions.explanation: Events can come from the user's actions, such as clicking or typing, from the system, such as a timer, and from the program itself. Since A, C and D can all generate events, All the options is the best answer.

questions.question: A structured chart is a

options.b: Document of what has to be done
options.d: A hierarchical partitioning of the program

questions.explanation: A structure chart shows a program broken down into its modules, arranged in levels (a hierarchy) from the main module down to smaller ones. It is not a programming language (A) or a requirements statement (E).

questions.question: The pseudocode is used for
questions.explanation: Pseudocode is used to write out the steps of a program in plain, English-like language before the real code is written. Coding and executing the program (D, E) happen later, and showing program flow as a diagram (C) is the job of a flowchart.

questions.question: Numbers with decimal points are called
questions.explanation: Numbers that have a decimal point, such as 3.14 or -0.5, are called real numbers. Integers (E) are whole numbers without a decimal point, and Boolean values (D) are just True or False.

questions.question: In VB data types, which of the following is correct

options.a: A variable with data type integer can always be assigned to another variable of data type long with no error
options.b: A variable with data type long can be assigned to another variable of data type integer with no error
options.c: Real is a special type of data type in VB
options.d: The integer and decimal data types have the same precision level

questions.explanation: A Long variable can hold every value an Integer can hold, so assigning an Integer to a Long never causes an error. Going the other way (B) can fail when the Long value is bigger than 32767, and Real (C) is not a VB data type.

questions.question: Which of the following data types is wrong?
questions.explanation: VB type-declaration characters are % (Integer), & (Long), $ (String), ! (Single), # (Double) and @ (Currency). The asterisk is not one of them, so TaxRate* is wrong.

questions.question: Constructs in which an IF block is contained inside another IF block are called?
questions.explanation: A nested IF is an IF block placed inside another IF block, so the inner test runs only when the outer test allows it. An IF...ELSE block (E) is a single decision with two paths, not one IF inside another.

questions.question: Which of the following is a control structure in Visual Basic?
questions.explanation: If...Then...Else is a control structure because it decides which statements run based on a condition. Print, Input and Output (B, C, D) are statements for showing or reading data, not structures that control the flow of a program.

questions.question: The purpose of a loop in programming is to:

options.a: Run a code block one time
options.b: Repeat a code block as needed

questions.explanation: A loop repeats a block of code as many times as needed or while a condition holds. Running code only once (A) needs no loop, and storing data (C) and showing results (D) are not what loops are for.

questions.question: In Visual Basic, which loop executes a block of code a specific number of times?
questions.explanation: A For...Next loop runs a block of code a set number of times using a counter, for example For i = 1 To 10. Do...Loop (A) and While...Wend (C) repeat while a condition holds, and If...Then (D) is a decision, not a loop.

questions.question: The "Else" part of an If...Then...Else statement is executed when:
questions.explanation: In an If...Then...Else statement, the Else part runs only when the condition is false. When the condition is true (A), the Then part runs instead.

questions.question: Which of the following is a selection structure in Visual Basic?
questions.explanation: Select Case is a selection structure: it picks one block of code to run from several choices based on a value. For...Next, Do...Loop and While...Wend (A, B, D) are repetition (loop) structures.

questions.question: A While...Wend loop continues to execute as long as:
questions.explanation: A While...Wend loop keeps repeating as long as its condition is true and stops once the condition becomes false. Option A has it backwards, and a loop does not simply run until the program ends (C).

questions.question: In Visual Basic, which statement is used to exit a loop prematurely?
questions.explanation: Exit For leaves a For...Next loop immediately, before all the iterations are finished (Exit Do does the same for Do loops). End If (B) just closes an If block, while Next (C) and Wend (D) mark the normal end of a loop's body.

questions.question: The purpose of a nested loop is to:

options.b: Embed a loop within another loop

questions.explanation: A nested loop is simply a loop placed inside the body of another loop, so the inner loop runs completely for every single pass of the outer loop. This is handy for work like going through rows and columns of a table. Option A describes an ordinary single loop, and options C and D have nothing to do with what nesting means.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a control structure in Visual Basic?
questions.explanation: Control structures decide the order in which statements run: selection (If...Then) and repetition (For...Next, Do...Loop). Print only sends output to the screen or printer; it does not change the flow of the program. Options A, B and C are all genuine control structures in Visual Basic.

questions.question: In Visual Basic, the "If" statement is used to:
questions.explanation: The If statement is a selection structure: it tests a condition and runs one block of code only when that condition is True (with Else covering the False case). Option A describes loops such as For...Next, option C is the job of variables and assignment, and option D is what output statements like Print or MsgBox do.

questions.question: A Do...Loop Until structure in Visual Basic executes until:
questions.explanation: In a Do...Loop Until structure, the body runs and the condition is checked at the bottom; the loop keeps repeating as long as the condition is False and stops as soon as it becomes True. Option B describes Do...Loop While, which is the opposite. Options C and D do not describe how the loop ends.

questions.question: The expression A < B means
questions.explanation: The < symbol is the 'less than' relational operator, so A < B is true when A is smaller than B. Option C reverses the meaning; that would be A > B. Option B says the same thing as A > B, and = and / (options A and E) are different operators.

questions.question:
A student gave the solution below as the program to add integers from 1 to 19.
1. Sub main()
2. Dim num, sum as integer
3. sum =0
4. for num= 1 to 19
5. writeline("enter the first number:"
6. num = readline()
7. sum = sum + num
8. Next
9. writeline("The sum is :" & sum)
10. End sub
Pick out the incorrect line(s) of code
questions.explanation: The loop variable num already counts from 1 to 19, so the program only needs sum = sum + num inside the loop. Lines 5 and 6 are wrong because they ask the user to type a number and overwrite num, which breaks the counting, and line 5 is also missing its closing bracket. Line 2 (Dim num, sum As Integer) and line 9 (printing the result) are valid, so options D and E are wrong.

questions.question:
A program to add the positive integers from 1 to 100 is given below:
1. Sub main()
2. Dim i, sum as integer
3. sum =0
4. For i= 1 to 100
5. sum = sum + [ ]
6. Next
7. writeline("Sum of 1 to 100 is:" & sum)
8. End sub
What is missing in [ ] on line 5?
questions.explanation: To add the integers from 1 to 100, each pass of the loop must add the current value of the counter i to the running total, so line 5 should read sum = sum + i. Using sum (option B) would just double the total each time. Using i-1 or i-2 (options D and E) would add the wrong numbers.

questions.question: One of the following is not an arithmetic operator in Visual Basic
questions.explanation: In Visual Basic, = is used for assignment and for comparing values (a relational operator), not for arithmetic. +, ^ and / (options A, D and E) are arithmetic operators for addition, exponentiation and division. MOD (option B) is also an arithmetic operator: it gives the remainder after division.

questions.question:
The following For-Next loop makes ____ passes.
Sum=0
For I= 1 to 20
Sum=Sum + 1
Next I
questions.explanation: A For loop from 1 to 20 with the default step of 1 runs once for each value 1, 2, 3, ... 20, which is 20 passes. Working: number of passes = 20 - 1 + 1 = 20. Option A (19) makes the common mistake of subtracting without adding 1, and option D (21) counts one pass too many.

questions.question: Another name for MOD (that is, modulus function) is
questions.explanation: MOD (the modulus operator) gives the remainder left after one integer is divided by another, so it is also called the integer remainder; for example 7 Mod 3 = 1. Integer division (option A) gives the whole-number quotient instead (7 \ 3 = 2). Options C, D and E are not names for MOD.

questions.question: (Evaluate the following expressions:) 2 mod 4 =
questions.explanation: Mod gives the remainder after division. Working: 2 divided by 4 is 0 with a remainder of 2, so 2 Mod 4 = 2. Option C (0) would only be right for a case like 4 Mod 2, where the division is exact. Remember that when the first number is smaller than the second, the remainder is the first number itself.

questions.question: (Evaluate the following expressions:) 9 mod 2^2 =
questions.explanation: Exponentiation (^) has higher precedence than Mod, so 2^2 is worked out first. Working: 2^2 = 4, then 9 Mod 4 = 1, because 9 = 2 x 4 + 1. Option A (2) or other answers come from ignoring the order of operations or from wrong remainders.

questions.question: (Evaluate the following expressions:) 4+3*6/2-5+5
questions.explanation: Multiplication and division are done before addition and subtraction, working left to right. Working: 3*6 = 18, 18/2 = 9, then 4 + 9 - 5 + 5 = 13. Option A (12) and the others come from doing the operations in the wrong order or from slips in the sums.

questions.question:
Given the following segment of code:
x=0
For i =1 To 5
x= x + i
Next i
What will be the final value of x?
questions.explanation: The loop adds each value of i from 1 to 5 to x, which starts at 0. Working: x = 0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15. Option B (14) misses one value and option E (16) adds one too many. Option D (55) is the sum of 1 to 10, not 1 to 5.

questions.question: (Evaluate the following expressions:) (2*3+4/2)> 3 AND 3<5 OR 10<9
questions.explanation: Work out the arithmetic first, then the comparisons, then AND, and OR last. Working: 2*3 + 4/2 = 8, so 8 > 3 is True; 3 < 5 is True; True AND True = True; 10 < 9 is False; True OR False = True. A logical expression gives True or False, so options C and D (numbers) cannot be right.

questions.question: (Evaluate the following expressions:) True AND True OR NOT False AND NOT True OR False =
questions.explanation: NOT is evaluated first, then AND, then OR. Working: NOT False = True and NOT True = False, so the expression becomes (True AND True) OR (True AND False) OR False = True OR False OR False = True. Option A (False) comes from ignoring precedence, and options D and E are impossible because the result cannot be both True and False.

questions.question: Another name for comparison operator is:
questions.explanation: Comparison operators such as =, <>, <, >, <= and >= are also called relational operators, because they test the relationship between two values and give True or False. Arithmetic operators (option A) do calculations, logical operators (option C) such as AND, OR and NOT combine True/False values, and options D and E are other kinds of operators.

questions.question: The operator <> signifies:
questions.explanation: In Visual Basic, <> means 'not equal to'; for example A <> B is True when A and B are different. That meaning does not appear among options A to D, which describe =, >, < and >=. So 'None of the above' is correct.

questions.question: Which operator is not in the class of operator below
questions.explanation: =, <=, >= and > are all relational (comparison) operators that compare two values and give True or False. The * symbol is an arithmetic operator for multiplication, so it does not belong to that class. Options A to D all belong together.

questions.question: The following is/are example(s) of logical operators:
questions.explanation: AND, OR and NOT are all logical operators, used to combine or reverse True/False conditions, for example (Age > 18) AND (Score >= 50). Options A, B and C each name only one of them, and option E leaves out NOT. Only option D includes all three.

questions.question: ____ is used to repeat a sequence of instructions for a particular number of times until certain condition(s) is(are) satisfied?
questions.explanation: Looping, also called iteration, repeats a set of instructions a given number of times or until a condition is met, using structures like For...Next and Do...Loop. Branching or decision (options A and E) chooses between paths but does not repeat them. Sequence (option C) runs statements once, in order.

questions.question: The result of 2^2 mod 6 is:
questions.explanation: Exponentiation is done before Mod, so 2^2 = 4 is worked out first. Working: 4 Mod 6 = 4, because 6 goes into 4 zero times with 4 left over. Option D (0) would need 4 to divide exactly by 6, and option A (2) ignores the exponent.

questions.question: In VB, the If...Else Statement is an example of
questions.explanation: If...Else is a selection (decision) control structure: it chooses which block of code to run depending on whether a condition is True or False. Iterative structures (option B) such as For...Next repeat code, and sequential structure (option A) just runs statements in order. 'Alternating' (option C) is not a standard name for a control structure.

questions.question: In VB the order of execution can take any of the following structures.
questions.explanation: Every program uses three basic structures. Sequential execution runs statements one after another, selective execution chooses between paths with If or Select Case, and iterative execution repeats steps with loops. Visual Basic supports all three, so options A, B and C alone are each incomplete.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a For loop and a Do... While loop?

options.a: For loops are used in COBOL, while Do... While is only used in VB
options.b: The For loop statement implicitly includes the incremental value while the Do... While does not
options.d: The Do... While statement implicitly includes the incremental value while the For loop does not

questions.explanation: A For...Next loop automatically increases its counter each time (by 1, or by the Step value), so the increment is built into the statement. In a Do...While loop the programmer must write the counter update inside the loop. Option D gets this the wrong way round, and options A and C are false.

questions.question: Amongst the following VB operations, which has the highest precedence
questions.explanation: In Visual Basic, exponentiation (^) has the highest precedence of the listed operations, so it is done before multiplication, division and Mod. Division (option A) and Mod (option D) come lower in the order. Logical operators (option B) such as AND and OR are evaluated last.

questions.question: In the code snippet below, what does STEP -1 mean? For index = 10 To 0 STEP -1

options.a: Divide the value of the index by 1
options.b: Nothing as For loops in VB cannot count backward
options.c: Reduce the value of the index by 1
options.d: It serves as entry point to the for loop

questions.explanation: Step -1 makes the For loop count down by 1 each pass, so the index goes 10, 9, 8, ... down to 0. Option B is wrong because For loops in Visual Basic can count backwards with a negative Step. The Step value is added to the counter; it does not divide it (option A).

questions.question: All these are iterative keywords except which?
questions.explanation: For, While and Next are used to build loops (iteration) in Visual Basic. Dim declares a variable and has nothing to do with repetition, so it is the exception. Options A, B and C all belong to loop structures.

questions.question: Which of the following is a recognized control structure in VB
questions.explanation: Control structures decide the order in which statements run, and the three basic ones are sequence, selection (decision) and iteration (looping). A picture box (B) is a VB control placed on a form, not a control structure, and options A, C and D are not VB control structures either.

questions.question: How many iterations are performed in the code snippet below: sum=0, i=10 / Do / sum = sum+i / i = i-2 / While (i >= 4)

options.e: The program will give an error and will not run

questions.explanation: Trace the loop: i = 10, 8, 6 and 4 each pass through the body, adding to sum, and after each pass i drops by 2. After the pass with i = 4, i becomes 2, the test i >= 4 fails, and the loop stops, so there are 4 iterations (sum = 28). Option A (5) wrongly counts i = 2.

questions.question: In the VB code snippet below, what does the statement STEP -5 mean: For counter = 0 to 100 STEP -5

options.a: Increase the value of the counter by 5 during each loop
options.b: After each loop reduce the value of the counter by 5
options.c: Before each loop reduce the value of the counter by 5
options.d: Before each loop increase the value of the counter by 5
options.e: Counting upwards from 0 to 100 yet reducing by 5 is not allowed in VB

questions.explanation: STEP sets how much the counter changes each time the loop goes round, so STEP -5 means the counter is reduced by 5 after each pass. With a start of 0 and an end of 100, counting down never reaches 100, so the loop body simply does not run, but the statement itself is still valid. That is why E is wrong, and A and D describe increasing the counter, which a negative step does not do.

questions.question: (2*3+4/2)> 3 AND 3<5 OR 10<9
questions.explanation: Work out the arithmetic first: 2*3 + 4/2 = 6 + 2 = 8, and 8 > 3 is True. Next, 3 < 5 is True, so True AND True = True. Finally, True OR (10 < 9 = False) gives True. Options C and D are numbers, but a comparison like this always gives True or False.

questions.question: True AND True OR NOT False AND NOT True OR False =
questions.explanation: Work out NOT first, then AND, then OR. NOT False = True and NOT True = False, so the expression becomes (True AND True) OR (True AND False) OR False, which is True OR False OR False = True. Option A is wrong because the first part, True AND True, is already True, and with OR one True part is enough to make the whole result True.

questions.question: which of the following is not an array declaration in Visual Basic
questions.explanation: 'Rate=[1...20];' uses square brackets, a dotted range and a semicolon, which is Pascal-style syntax, not Visual Basic. The other options all follow the VB pattern of Dim, the array name and its size in round brackets, optionally followed by As and a data type, as in Dim K(10) As Integer.

questions.question: which of the following is not an example of a loop statement in V.B
questions.explanation: If...Else is a decision statement: it checks a condition once and chooses which block of code to run, but it never repeats anything. Do...While, For Each...Next and While...Wend (B, C, D) all repeat a block of code, so they are loop statements, which also rules out E.

questions.question: What are dynamic arrays?

options.b: They are arrays that are portable
options.d: Arrays whose size can be changed at various places within a program

questions.explanation: A dynamic array is one whose size can be changed while the program runs, using the ReDim statement. It has nothing to do with being mobile or portable (A, B).

questions.question: which is not a declarative statement in dynamic arrays
questions.explanation: Dynamic arrays are declared with Dim, Public or Private (and later resized with ReDim). '.X' is not a Visual Basic keyword at all, so it is the one that is not a declaration statement.

questions.question: Subscripted variables are.....

options.c: Variables declared without a data type

questions.explanation: A subscripted variable is one individual element of an array, picked out by its subscript (index), such as Marks(3). Option A describes the whole array rather than a single element, and a variable declared without a data type (C) is simply a Variant, not a subscripted variable.

questions.question: Which operator performs two operations
questions.explanation: In Visual Basic the + operator has two jobs: it adds numbers (2 + 3 gives 5) and it also joins strings ("Good" + "day" gives "Goodday"). The *, / and - operators (B, C, D) are used for arithmetic, and & (E) is used only for joining strings.

questions.question: What value would be store in 25-8/2+2
questions.explanation: Division is done before addition and subtraction, so 8/2 = 4 is worked out first. Then 25 - 4 + 2 is evaluated left to right, giving 21 + 2 = 23. Option B (21) forgets the final + 2.

questions.question: How is the following algebraic expression represented in VB 2(x+3y)?
questions.explanation: VB never assumes multiplication, so every product needs an asterisk: 2(x+3y) becomes 2*(x+3*y). Option A leaves out the * after the 2, and E (2*x+3*y) drops the brackets, which changes the value because only x would be doubled.

questions.question: Given 7.7\1.7 in VB, what is the result of this expression?
questions.explanation: The backslash (\) is VB's integer division operator: it first rounds both numbers to whole numbers and then divides, dropping any remainder. So 7.7 rounds to 8 and 1.7 rounds to 2, and 8 \ 2 = 4. Option C (4.53) is what ordinary division (/) would give.

questions.question: The following are logical operators except:
questions.explanation: Not, Imp, Eqv and And are all VB logical operators used to combine or reverse True/False conditions. But is an ordinary English word, not a VB operator.

questions.question: The following are valid relational operators in VB except:
questions.explanation: VB tests equality with a single equals sign (=), and uses <, > and <> for less than, greater than and not equal. The double equals (==) comes from languages like C and Java and is not valid in VB.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a valid looping statement in VB?
questions.explanation: For-Next, Do-Loop and While-Wend are the looping structures in VB. With is used to work with several properties of one object, not to repeat code, so While-With is not a loop at all.

questions.question: Looping in VB is divided into 2 categories. They are:
questions.explanation: Some loops run a fixed, known number of times (unconditional, like For-Next), while others keep going until a condition changes (conditional, like Do-Loop). That gives the two categories conditional and unconditional; the other pairs mix in terms that do not describe looping.

questions.question: For what type of application is the Select Case structure well-suited?
questions.explanation: Select Case picks one block of code from several based on a single value, which matches a menu where the user chooses one numbered option. That is why it suits menu-driven applications. Options A, B, C and E describe other kinds of programs and do not capture this one-choice-from-a-list idea.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct format for If-Then statements?

options.a: If executable expression Then logical statement
options.b: If logical statement Then executable expression
options.c: If logical expression Then executable statement
options.d: If conditional statement Then logical expression
options.e: If executable statement Then logical expression

questions.explanation: The If-Then form is: If logical expression Then executable statement. The condition after If must be a logical expression that is True or False, and what follows Then is the statement to run. Options A, B, D and E swap or misname these parts.

questions.question: Select-Case structure offers a simple solution to several ............... If-Then-Else or If-Then-ElseIf-Else blocks:
questions.explanation: Select Case offers a simple replacement for several competing If-Then-Else or If-Then-ElseIf blocks, that is, blocks that each test a different possibility. The other words (completing, completion, competition, competent) do not fit the meaning of the sentence.

questions.question:
The following For-Next loop makes ............. passes
Sum = 0
For I = 1 to 10
Sum = Sum + I
Next I
questions.explanation: The loop counter I takes the values 1, 2, 3, ... 10, and the loop body runs once for each value. That is 10 passes. Option E (11) wrongly counts the final step where I becomes 11 and the loop stops.

questions.question: The last clause in a Select Case structure, used when no other case matches, is:
questions.explanation: Case Else is the final clause in a Select Case block; it runs when the value does not match any of the earlier Case tests, and then End Select closes the block. Plain Case (E) is used for the earlier tests, and Case If, Case Or and Or Case (A, B, C) are not valid Visual Basic clauses.

questions.question: How many different ways can a Do-Loop structure be written?
questions.explanation: A Do loop can test its condition with While or Until, and the test can go at the top or the bottom: Do While...Loop, Do Until...Loop, Do...Loop While and Do...Loop Until. That makes 4 forms. Option E (2) counts only While and Until without the two positions.

questions.question: A While...Wend loop is similar to a:
questions.explanation: While...Wend repeats its statements as long as a condition is True and checks the condition at the start, which is exactly how Do While...Loop works. Do...Until (B) repeats until a condition becomes True, and For...Next (A) runs a counted number of times.

questions.question: To execute a statement or a group of statements for a False expression, the .......... Operator is used
questions.explanation: Not reverses a condition, so Not (expression) is True when the expression is False. That lets you run statements for a False result. And (D) combines two conditions, and But, No and Nor are not VB operators.

questions.question: To handle both True and False conditions a ........... statement is used in conjunction with an If statement
questions.explanation: Else gives an If statement a second branch: the If part runs when the condition is True and the Else part runs when it is False. Next (A) ends a For loop, and Or (C) joins two conditions rather than adding a False branch.

questions.question: The key feature of a conditional loop is the.......
questions.explanation: A conditional loop keeps repeating only while (or until) a condition is met, so the condition is its key feature. A statement or expression (A, C) is just part of any program, and a relational statement (D) is only one way of writing a condition.

questions.question: The three most frequently used logical operators in VB are:
questions.explanation: And, Or and Not are the logical operators used most often in VB to combine or reverse conditions. Imp and Eqv (in A, B and D) do exist but are rarely used, and If (D) is not an operator at all.

questions.question: Given that the numeric variable n = 4 and the string variable answ = "Y", which of the following conditions is false?
questions.explanation: With n = 4, the test n < 6 is True, so Not (n < 6) is False. Option A is True (4 is between 2 and 6), C is True because 2 < 4, D is True because "Y" is not equal to lowercase "y", and E is True because answ = "Y".

questions.question: The use of parentheses with logical operators improves....... of program
questions.explanation: Brackets make it clear which parts of a logical expression are grouped together, so a reader can follow the program more easily. That is readability. Beauty and loveliness (B, D) are not programming qualities, and brackets do not by themselves make a program consistent or complete.

questions.question: A For statement designates the use of a .............. variable that is initialized and automatically changes after the each execution of loop.
questions.explanation: A For statement uses a control (counter) variable that is given a starting value and changes automatically, by the step amount, after each pass of the loop. The other words do not describe this loop counter.

questions.question: Given that the numeric variables a and b are 4 and 3, respectively, and the string values c and d are "hello" and "bye" respectively, which of the following conditions is false?
questions.explanation: With c = "hello" and d = "bye", the expression "good" & d gives "goodbye", and "hello" < "goodbye" is False because h comes after g. Option A is True (7 < 8), B is True (5 - 3 = 2 and 4/2 = 2), and E is True (3 < 4).

questions.question: The two major types of control statements are:
questions.explanation: Control statements either choose which code to run (branching, such as If and Select Case) or repeat code (looping, such as For and Do). The other pairs use made-up terms like scoring, doubling and choosing.

questions.question: Logical expressions are either....
questions.explanation: A logical expression is a condition, and it can only have one of two values: True or False. Words like probable, possible or distinct (A, B, C) are not values a condition can take.

questions.question:
[Use the information below to answer this question. Given a loop that generates every fifth integer, beginning with I = 1 and continuing for all integers that are less than 150.]
How many integers would be generated?
questions.explanation: The loop generates 1, 6, 11, ..., adding 5 each time while the value is below 150. The last value is 146 = 1 + 5 x 29, so there are 29 + 1 = 30 integers. Option B (29) forgets to count the starting value 1.

questions.question:
[Use the information below to answer this question. Given a loop that generates every fifth integer, beginning with I = 1 and continuing for all integers that are less than 150.]
What would be the sum of those integers that are evenly divisible by 6?
questions.explanation: The generated numbers are 1, 6, 11, ..., 146, and those divisible by 6 are 6, 36, 66, 96 and 126. Their sum is 6 + 36 + 66 + 96 + 126 = 330. The other options do not match this total.

questions.question:
[Use the information below to answer this question. Given a loop that generates every fifth integer, beginning with I = 1 and continuing for all integers that are less than 150.]
What would be the value of I that will cause the loop to terminate?
questions.explanation: Starting at 1 and adding 5 each time gives 1, 6, 11, ..., 141, 146, and the next value is 146 + 5 = 151. Because 151 is not less than 150, it is the value that stops the loop. Option C (146) is the last value used inside the loop, not the one that ends it, and 149, 150 and 152 are never produced by this counting pattern.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid Visual Basic conditional statement?
questions.explanation: A complete VB condition needs each comparison written in full, joined by a logical operator: (2 < n) Or (n < 5). Option A is missing the n before < 5, C uses ^, which is the power operator, and D and E do not form two complete comparisons.

questions.question: Consider the code inside this bracket: (For i = 0 to 7 step 2 Print "blast off" Next i). How many times will the code section above execute the print statement?
questions.explanation: With Step 2, the counter i takes the values 0, 2, 4 and 6; the next value, 8, is beyond 7, so the loop stops. That is 4 times through the loop, so the print statement runs 4 times. Option E (8) counts every number from 0 to 7 as if the step were 1.

questions.question: Which of these have highest precedence?
questions.explanation: Brackets () have the highest precedence, so whatever is inside them is worked out first. Multiplication (D) comes before addition (A), and ++ and >> (B, E) are operators from languages like C, which are still evaluated after brackets.

questions.question: Which Case clause will be true whenever the value of the selector in a Select Case block is between 1 and 5 or is 8?
questions.explanation: In Select Case, a range is written with To and separate values are listed with commas, so Case 1 To 5, 8 matches 1 through 5 or 8. Option C (Case 1 To 8) would also match 6 and 7, and E uses a semicolon, which is not allowed.

questions.question: Which of the following protocols is used for WWW?
questions.explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the protocol used to request and send web pages on the World Wide Web. Option E, FTP, is used for transferring files, not for browsing web pages. Option A, W3, is just a nickname for the web, and option D, NetWare, is a network operating system.

questions.question: What does the 'www' stand for in a web address?
questions.explanation: In a web address, 'www' stands for World Wide Web, the system of linked web pages reached over the internet. Options B and E leave out a word or put the words in the wrong order, and options A and C are not what the letters stand for.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid domain name?
questions.explanation: www.computer.com is a valid domain name, with parts separated by dots and ending in a top-level domain such as .com. Options A, B, D and E contain slashes or @ signs placed where they are not allowed, which breaks domain name rules.

questions.question: Which device is required for the Internet connection?
questions.explanation: A modem is the device that connects a home computer to the Internet, converting the computer's digital signals so they can travel over telephone or cable lines. A joystick (A) is for games, a CD drive (C) reads discs and a printer (D) produces hard copy, so none of them provides an Internet link.

questions.question: Which one does not belong in the group?
questions.explanation: Unix is an operating system, while Google Chrome, Opera, Firefox and Internet Explorer are all web browsers. That makes Unix the odd one out.

questions.question: The internet was developed in the ______
questions.explanation: The Internet grew out of ARPANET, which was developed in the late 1960s and first linked computers in 1969. TCP/IP and wider use came in the 1970s and 1980s (C and D), but those were stages in the growth of a network that had already started.

questions.question: Which of the following is an Internet service?
questions.explanation: Email is a service delivered over the Internet, letting people send and receive messages between computers anywhere in the world. Word processing, spreadsheets and image editing (options A, C and D) are application programs that run on your own computer and work fine without any Internet connection.

questions.question: The Internet is:

options.b: A global network of interconnected systems

questions.explanation: The Internet is a worldwide network of networks, linking millions of computers and smaller networks so they can exchange data. It is not controlled from one central point, so option A is wrong. Options C and D describe a single computer and a piece of software, not a network.

questions.question: A browser is used to:
questions.explanation: A web browser such as Chrome, Firefox or Edge is the program you use to request, display and navigate web pages. Writing code (option A) is done in an editor or IDE, saving files locally (option C) is handled by the operating system and storage devices, and option D is the CPU's job.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a protocol?
questions.explanation: A protocol is an agreed set of rules for how data is communicated, and HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the protocol that carries web pages between servers and browsers. The CPU, RAM and ROM (options A, C and D) are hardware parts of the computer, not sets of communication rules.

questions.question: The term "upload" refers to:

options.b: Sending data to a remote server

questions.explanation: Uploading means sending data from your own computer to a remote computer or server, for example posting a photo or submitting an assignment online. Option A, retrieving data from the web, is downloading, which is the opposite direction. Options C and D describe deleting and browsing, not transferring data.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to transfer email?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is the standard protocol used to send and relay email between mail servers. HTTP (option A) carries web pages and FTP (option C) transfers files. TCP (option D) is a lower-level protocol that moves packets for many services, but it is not the email protocol itself.

questions.question: The World Wide Web (WWW) is:

options.a: A set of linked documents online

questions.explanation: The World Wide Web is the huge collection of web pages and other documents linked together by hyperlinks and accessed over the Internet with a browser. Option B describes the Internet itself, the physical network that the Web runs on. The Web is not a programming standard or a network layout, so options C and D are wrong.

questions.question: Which of the following is a search engine?
questions.explanation: Google is a search engine: it indexes web pages and lets you find them by typing keywords. Excel (option A) is a spreadsheet, Photoshop (option C) is a graphics editor, and Notepad (option D) is a simple text editor; none of them search the web.

questions.question: A website's address is also known as its:
questions.explanation: A website's address is its URL (Uniform Resource Locator), for example https://www.unilag.edu.ng, which tells the browser exactly where to find the resource. An IP address (option A) is the numeric address of a machine, not the web address people type. A protocol (option C) is a set of communication rules, and a bookmark folder (option D) only stores saved links.

questions.question: Which of the following is a risk of using the Internet?
questions.explanation: Being connected to the Internet exposes computers to threats such as viruses, hacking, phishing and other cyberattacks, which is a real risk. Options A, C and D (fast messaging, access to knowledge and working together across distances) are all benefits of the Internet, not risks.

questions.question: The term "download" refers to:
questions.explanation: Downloading means receiving data from a remote computer or the web and saving it onto your own device, for example getting a PDF from a website. Option A, sending data outward, is uploading. Option C is deleting, and option D describes saving in general, not receiving it from the web.

questions.question: Which protocol is used for secure communication on the Internet?
questions.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP with encryption (using SSL/TLS), so data passing between your browser and the website cannot easily be read by others; that is why banking and login pages use it. Plain HTTP (option A) is not encrypted. FTP and SMTP (options B and D) are for file transfer and sending email, and in their basic forms they are not secure either.

questions.question: The .net domain is used for ____.
questions.explanation: .net is a top-level domain originally created for organisations involved in networking, such as Internet service providers and network infrastructure companies. Educational institutions use .edu (option A), international organisations use .int (option B), and commercial (profit-making) organisations traditionally use .com (option C).

questions.question: The world wide web was invented by ____.
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN, creating HTTP, HTML and the first web browser. Steve Jobs (option A) co-founded Apple, Bill Gates (option B) co-founded Microsoft, Larry Ellison (option D) co-founded Oracle, and Charles Babbage (option E) designed mechanical computing engines in the 1800s.

questions.question: Which of these is a mail transfer protocol?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is the protocol used to send and transfer email between mail servers. HTML (option B) is used to write web pages, XML (option D) is a data markup language, and UML (option C) is a diagram language for designing software. 'XTML' (option E) is not a real standard.

questions.question: The transfer of data from a local computer to a remote computer is ____.
questions.explanation: Uploading is the transfer of data from your own (local) computer to a remote computer, such as a web server. Downloading (option A) is the reverse, moving data from the remote computer to yours. 'Loading', 'posting' and 'copying' (options B, C and D) are not the technical terms for this direction of transfer.

questions.question: ____ is an online discussion group that does not send direct E-mail to members.
questions.explanation: Usenet is a worldwide system of discussion groups (newsgroups) where messages are posted to a shared server and members go and read them; nothing is mailed directly to them. A Listserv (option A) is a mailing list that does send each message to members' email inboxes. Telnet and Gopher (options B and E) are older Internet services, and a Petri net (option D) is a mathematical model.

questions.question: Which of this is a metasearch engine?
questions.explanation: A metasearch engine does not keep its own index; it sends your query to several other search engines at once and combines their results, and Dogpile works this way. Google, Yahoo, Lycos and Ask (options A to D) are ordinary search engines or portals that search their own indexes.

questions.question: A self contained program that affects computers over a network is called ____.
questions.explanation: A worm is a self-contained program that copies itself and spreads across a network on its own, without needing to attach to another file. A virus (option A) is not self-contained: it attaches itself to a host program or file and spreads when that file is run. A Trojan (option D) pretends to be useful software and does not replicate itself, and 'bacteria' (option B) is not the standard term.

questions.question: ____ is a language for describing web pages.
questions.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the language used to describe the structure and content of web pages. HTTP (option A) is the protocol that transfers those pages, FTP (option B) transfers files, TCP/IP (option C) is the basic Internet communication protocol, and DNS (option D) translates domain names into IP addresses.

questions.question: Which of this is not a search engine?
questions.explanation: Safari is Apple's web browser, a program for viewing web pages, not a search engine. Yahoo, Google, Ask and Bing (options A, C, D and E) are all search engines that help you find information on the web. A browser is the program you use to reach a search engine.

questions.question: A personal article posted on the web for public access is called ____.
questions.explanation: A blog (short for weblog) is a personal online journal or article that its owner posts on the web for anyone to read. Usenet (option B) is a system of discussion newsgroups, chat (option D) is a live text conversation, and email (option E) is sent privately to particular people. 'News watch' (option A) is not a standard term for this.

questions.question: The primary purpose of the internet is ____.
questions.explanation: The Internet was created so that computers and people could share information and resources, and that remains its primary purpose. Entertainment, chatting and business (options B, C and D) are popular uses, but they all come from that basic ability to share information. That is why 'All of the above' (option E) does not name the primary purpose.

questions.question: An underlined word on a web page is usually a(n) ____.
questions.explanation: On web pages, underlined (often blue) text usually marks a hyperlink, which takes you to another page or resource when you click it. It is not a mistake or simply an important word (options A and B). The text of a link can be anything, so it is not necessarily a web address (option D).

questions.question: Another name for a URL is?
questions.explanation: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is commonly called a web address, for example https://www.google.com. An ISP is an Internet Service Provider, not an address (option A), and 'IPS address' (option C) is not a standard term. A website (option D) is the collection of pages that the URL points to, not the address itself.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to find information on the web?
questions.explanation: Search engines, web directories (subject-sorted lists of sites) and online databases are all tools for finding information on the web. Since a search engine and a directory both clearly work, no single option A, B or C can be the full answer. 'All of the above' covers every valid tool.

questions.question: A set of commands used to create web documents
questions.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the set of commands, called tags, used to create web documents. The WWW (option A) is the collection of linked pages, a browser (option D) is software for viewing them, and Telnet and FTP (options B and E) are services for remote login and file transfer.

questions.question: A software that allows you to access the web
questions.explanation: A web browser is the software that lets you access and view pages on the World Wide Web, for example Chrome or Firefox. HTML (option C) is the language pages are written in, the WWW (option A) is the content itself, and Telnet and FTP (options B and E) are other Internet services.

questions.question: A collection of websites that can be accessed by using hypertext interface
questions.explanation: The World Wide Web (WWW) is the collection of websites and pages linked together by hypertext, reached through a browser. HTML (option C) is the language used to build those pages, and a browser (option D) is the tool used to view them. Telnet and FTP (options B and E) are not hypertext systems.

questions.question: Used to transfer files from host to host
questions.explanation: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is the service used to copy files from one host computer to another across a network. Telnet (option B) is for logging in remotely, not moving files. The WWW, HTML and the browser (options A, C and D) are about web pages.

questions.question: Allows remote login to another computer
questions.explanation: Telnet lets a user log in to a remote computer and work on it as if sitting at its terminal. FTP (option E) only transfers files and does not give you a working session on the other machine. The WWW, HTML and browsers (options A, C and D) deal with web pages.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a social networking application?
questions.explanation: Facebook, Twitter, Google+ and MySpace (options A to D) were all social networking applications, letting users create profiles, connect with friends and share posts. Since every option listed is a social network, 'None of the above' is correct. Google+ was later shut down, but it was a social network.

questions.question: The number of computers in the internet is
questions.explanation: The Internet has no fixed number of computers; devices join and leave all the time, and the total runs into many millions. Options A and C give small fixed figures, and option D is wrong because the number keeps changing.

questions.question: Unwanted mail coming with your electronic e-mail is termed
questions.explanation: Spam is unwanted, unsolicited email, usually advertising or scams sent to many people at once. A virus (option D) is harmful code that may arrive by email, but the term for unwanted mail itself is spam. Intrusion (option A) means unauthorised access to a system, and option C is not a real term.

questions.question: Some benefits of the Internet are
questions.explanation: The Internet allows communication through email, chat and calls, data interchange (sharing files and information), and money transfer through online banking and payment services. Since all three are real benefits, 'All of these' is correct. Options A, B and C alone are each incomplete.

questions.question: FTP is an acronym for
questions.explanation: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol, the standard set of rules for copying files between computers over a network. 'Teleprocessing' (options A and B) is not part of the name. Option D uses 'Transmission' instead of the correct word 'Transfer'.

questions.question: All the following are common web browsers EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: ARPAnet was an early research network that grew into the Internet; it was never a web browser. Safari, Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox (options B, C and D) are all web browsers people use to view websites.

questions.question: URL stands for:
questions.explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, the address that identifies a particular page or file on the web, such as a website address. The other expansions are distractors with the wrong words in place of "Resource" or "Locator".

questions.question: In what year was ARPAnet developed?
questions.explanation: ARPAnet was developed by the US Department of Defense's research agency and went live in 1969, linking a few university computers. It later grew into the Internet. The 1970s and 1980s (B and C) saw it expand, but its development dates to 1969.

questions.question: The quantity of data, text, voice, video etc. that can be sent via a Communication channel at a time through the internet is called
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the amount of data a communication channel can carry at a time, and it is usually measured in bits per second. A packet (A) is just one small unit of the data being sent, not the capacity of the channel.

questions.question: TCP means
questions.explanation: TCP stands for Transmission Control Protocol, the Internet protocol that breaks data into packets and makes sure they arrive complete and in order. The other options change "Transmission" or "Control" into wrong words.

questions.question: All of the following are web browsers except
questions.explanation: Unix is an operating system, not a web browser. Firefox, Internet Explorer, Google Chrome and Opera (A, B, D, E) are all browsers used for viewing websites.

questions.question:
[Match each term with the description that fits best in the next five (5) questions: a Gopher; b URL; c HTML; d TCP/IP; e FTP]
A specific Internet communication protocol for transferring programs and long data files.
questions.explanation: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is the Internet protocol used for moving programs and large data files between computers. TCP/IP (D) is the general set of protocols for addressing and sending data, not the specific one for file transfer.

questions.question:
[Match each term with the description that fits best in the next five (5) questions: a Gopher; b URL; c HTML; d TCP/IP; e FTP]
The language used to format web pages.
questions.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) uses tags to format and structure web pages. A URL (B) is only the address of a page, not the language used to build it.

questions.question:
[Match each term with the description that fits best in the next five (5) questions: a Gopher; b URL; c HTML; d TCP/IP; e FTP]
The Internet's standard protocols for addressing and formatting transmissions.
questions.explanation: TCP/IP is the standard set of Internet protocols: IP handles addressing and routing, while TCP breaks data into packets and makes sure it is delivered correctly. FTP (E) is a single protocol built on top of TCP/IP just for file transfer.

questions.question:
[Match each term with the description that fits best in the next five (5) questions: a Gopher; b URL; c HTML; d TCP/IP; e FTP]
A Web address identifying a specific Internet document.
questions.explanation: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the web address that points to one specific document or resource on the Internet. HTML (C) is the language the document is written in, not its address.

questions.question:
[Match each term with the description that fits best in the next five (5) questions: a Gopher; b URL; c HTML; d TCP/IP; e FTP]
An electronic catalogue of Internet resources organised in a hierarchy.
questions.explanation: Gopher was an early Internet system that organised resources into a hierarchy of menus, like a catalogue you could browse level by level. It was used before the World Wide Web became popular. A URL (B) points to just one resource.

questions.question: For a computer to be connected to the Internet through a dial-up telephone line, you need the following, EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Connecting a computer to the Internet over a dial-up line needs a modem, a telephone line and suitable communication software. A pager is a separate one-way messaging gadget and plays no part in making the connection, so it is the exception. Options A, B and C are all needed.

questions.question: The basic language for creating web sites on the Internet is
questions.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the basic language used to build web pages, using tags to describe headings, text, links and images. COBOL (A) is a business programming language, and Visual Basic and Pascal (B, D) are general programming languages, not web page languages.

questions.question: To link one page on the web to another you should use
questions.explanation: A hyperlink is a clickable link that takes you from one web page to another. Hypertext (C) is text that contains links, while GOTO (A) is a programming statement.

questions.question: e-business includes which of the following:
questions.explanation: E-business covers all business done electronically, including e-commerce (buying and selling online), EDI (exchanging business documents between computers) and EFT (moving money electronically). Since A, B and C are all part of it, D is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is Not available on the Internet?
questions.explanation: FTP (file transfer), Gopher (menu-based document search), the World Wide Web and e-mail (A to D) are all Internet services. Since none of them is missing from the Internet, the answer is 'none of these'.

questions.question: You have sent an e-mail to a friend in London, on arrival at destination, the recipient's computer is shut down. The e-mail would therefore be

options.e: changed to a utility program and kept in the ROM

questions.explanation: E-mail is stored on the recipient's mail server, in their mailbox, so it waits there until they switch on and check their mail. It is not destroyed or sent back (A, B) just because their computer is off.

questions.question: Before your browser can connect to a website, you must first supply the
questions.explanation: To open a website, the browser needs its address, the URL (Uniform Resource Locator), such as www.example.com. An e-mail address (A) is for sending mail, not for finding websites.

questions.question: Identify the true statement here

options.a: a page can contains many web sites
options.b: a page must contain only one website
options.c: a website can contain many web pages
options.d: contents of a web page cannot be altered
options.e: a web page cannot contain coloured pictures

questions.explanation: A website is a collection of related web pages under one address, so one website can contain many pages. The reverse (A, B) is wrong, and web pages can be updated (D) and can include coloured pictures (E).

questions.question: When you surf the Internet, the hand symbol that carries you from one page or website to another is
questions.explanation: When you hover over a hyperlink, the pointer usually changes to a hand, and clicking it takes you to another page or website. Gopher (A) is an old menu-based search service and spam (D) is unwanted e-mail.

questions.question: This command or program connects you to remote computers in the Internet.
questions.explanation: Telnet is the program and protocol for logging in to and using a remote computer over the Internet. ARPANET (C) was the early network that grew into the Internet, not a command.

questions.question: In HTML, the tags that tell the browser how to display the page is
questions.explanation: HTML is a markup language, and its markup tags are the instructions in a web page that tell the browser how to structure and display the content. Head and body (B, E) are only two sections of a page, style (D) is one particular tag for formatting, and foot (C) is not a standard HTML section tag.

questions.question: ARPANET stands for?
questions.explanation: ARPANET stands for Advanced Research Projects Agency Network, the US network that grew into the internet. The other options replace Agency with words like Automatic or Authorized, which are not part of the name.

questions.question: What is internet?
questions.explanation: The internet is a worldwide network of networks: many separate networks connected together so they can exchange data. Options B to E name only devices or one type of connection, not networks linked to each other.

questions.question: In reality, Internet Protocol recognizes only
questions.explanation: The Internet Protocol (IP) moves data using IP addresses only; it does not deal with names or physical locations. MAC addresses (B) are used inside a local network, and postal addresses (A) have nothing to do with IP.

questions.question: Highlighted words that links to other documents or page is called
questions.explanation: Hypertext is highlighted text that you click to jump to another document or page. Pointers, linkers and supertext (A, C, E) are not the name for this, and a reference (D) is just a general word for pointing to other material.

questions.question: The equipment needed to allow home computers connect to the Internet is called a
questions.explanation: A modem connects a home computer to the internet by converting the computer's digital signals into a form that can travel over telephone or cable lines and back again. A gateway (A) links different networks, while a monitor and mouse (C, E) are ordinary peripherals.

questions.question: A temporary memory where copies of any pages that the user has viewed is stored
questions.explanation: A cache is a temporary memory that keeps copies of recently used data, and a web browser's cache keeps copies of pages you have viewed so they load faster next time. RAM (C) is general working memory, and ROM (D) holds fixed start-up instructions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using a bookmark in a web browser?

options.a: To save favourite websites for easy access
options.c: To download files from a remote computer
options.d: To translate a web page into HTML

questions.explanation: A bookmark saves the address of a website in your browser so you can return to it quickly later, which is why it is used for favourite sites. Blocking unwanted e-mail (B) is the job of a spam filter, and copying files from a remote computer (C) is downloading.

questions.question: WWW means
questions.explanation: WWW stands for World Wide Web, the system of linked web pages you reach through the internet. The other options are word plays that are not the real name.

questions.question: ARPAnet initially connected four major mainframe computers located in
questions.explanation: ARPANET's first four connected computers were at UCLA, the Stanford Research Institute and UC Santa Barbara in California, and the University of Utah. So the locations were California and Utah.

questions.question: The following are merits of decentralization of the internet except

options.a: Regulation of objectionable content is almost impossible
options.d: Any network of individual computer can join the internet and be treated as an equal

questions.explanation: The fact that objectionable content is almost impossible to regulate is a drawback of the internet's decentralized design, not a merit. Having no central computer, shared authority and equal treatment for any network that joins (B, C, D) are its benefits.
